# PR Discussion History

_Previous review discussions for PR #695._

## Review Threads (Inline Comments)

### Thread 1 — `js/smAgent.js`

**ai-teammate** (2026-10-04):
🚨 **BLOCKING: the scan flags a required context as CANCELLED even when a NEWER run already re-stamped it green**

`cancelledRequiredContexts` treats the context as cancelled if **any** check run in the commit's rollup reads `CANCELLED`:

```js
rollup.forEach(function (r) {
    var name = r && (r.name || r.context);
    var concl = r && r.conclusion ? String(r.conclusion).toUpperCase() : null;
    if (name && concl === 'CANCELLED' && contexts.indexOf(name) !== -1) {
        cancelled[name] = true;
    }
});
```

`github_get_commit_check_runs` returns **all** check runs on the commit (verified live: "Get all check runs ... for a commit SHA") — including stale ones from earlier attempts/dispatches. Branch protection resolves each required context by its **latest** check run; this code does not, despite the comment claiming "the check-runs rollup is the source of truth".

Reachable sequence with this repo's own machinery:

1. Validation run A (attempt 1) on head H is cancelled — exactly the #632/#682 class this rule targets (or stale-run cleanup).
2. `revalidate-armed` re-dispatches a fresh run B on H after the 15-min grace → B re-stamps `static`/`gate`/`agents-gate` **green**.
3. Next tick this rule runs **first** (before `merge-validated`), sees A's stale `CANCELLED` check runs, and `gh run rerun`s A + posts the marker — on a head that is already green and mergeable.

Consequences: the merge is delayed a full validation cycle; if the spurious rerun fails (moved base, flake), the freshly re-stamped red hands the PR to `fail_validation` and it gets parked — the rule actively harms the PRs it protects. Same trap after the rule's own remedy: attempt-1 cancelled check runs persist next to attempt-2's, so any tick where the marker read errors (`catch` → `rcReported = false`) re-fires.

Fix (~5 lines): keep only the **latest** check run per required context (max `completed_at`, tie-break by `id`) before testing `=== 'CANCELLED'`, and add a test fixture with a stale-cancelled + fresh-green pair (the current fixtures only ever carry the cancelled runs, which pins the bug).

---

### Thread 2 — `js/smAgent.js`

**ai-teammate** (2026-10-04):
⚠️ **IMPORTANT: once-per-head marker is posted even when the rerun set covers only part of the cancelled contexts**

`rcTargets` can legitimately cover a **subset** of `rcCancelled`: contexts whose cancelled runs are already attempt-2+ (skipped by design), or whose job names don't match any walked run (`jobs?per_page=50` cap, job-name/context drift). The marker is then posted anyway, and from the next tick on the `rcReported` check short-circuits **before** the mapping probe — the head is "remedied" forever while the uncovered contexts still read `CANCELLED` (the exact gh-682 BLOCKED symptom), and even the per-tick `"no rerunnable ... skip"` warn disappears into the marker.

```js
if (rcReported) {
    console.log('  ⏭️  ' + key + ' cancelled checks already re-run for head — waiting on the rerun');
    continue;
}
```

Suggestion: post the marker only when `rcTargets` covers **all** of `rcCancelled` (or list the uncovered contexts in the marker text), so an unmapped context keeps visibly retrying/warning instead of being silently latched shut by a partial remediation. Test to add: two cancelled contexts where only one maps to an attempt-1 run → no marker on that tick.

---

### Thread 3 — `js/unit-tests/test_smAgent.js`

**ai-teammate** (2026-10-04):
⚠️ **IMPORTANT: copy-paste bug in the new test helper — `it[k] = extra` drops the `[k]` index**

```js
function prItem682(n, extra) {
    var it = { key: 'pr-' + n, labels: ['ai_validating'], issueNumber: null,
               prNumber: n, draft: false, branch: 'ai/gh-1202',
               pr: { headSha: '898efd4' } };
    if (extra) { for (var k in extra) { if (extra.hasOwnProperty(k)) it[k] = extra; } }
    return it;
}
```

Every sibling helper in this file does `it[k] = extra[k]` (lines 855, 1682, 1864, 2041) — this copy assigns the whole `extra` object to every key. It is latent today only because every call site is `prItem682(1202)`; the first caller that passes `extra` (e.g. `prItem682(1202, { labels: ['ai_validated'] })`) gets `{ labels: {labels: [...]}, prNumber: {labels: [...]}, ... }` and a silently wrong fixture. One-character fix.

---

### Thread 4 — `js/smAgent.js`

**ai-teammate** (2026-10-04):
💡 **SUGGESTION: `number:` vs `pullRequestId:` — keep one spelling per tool in this file**

This new call site passes `number: ticket.prNumber` to `github_get_pr_comments`, while all 8 other call sites in this file (1573, 1817, 1845, 1993, 2020, 2165, 2979 …) use `pullRequestId:`. Both aliases work against the current dmtools runtime (verified live), but if the tool ever tightens its input schema, every site should already agree — `pullRequestId` is the canonical name per `js/common/trackers.js` ("the number argument keeps the tool's canonical pullRequestId name"). Same payload, just match the file's existing contract.

---

### Thread 5 — `js/smAgent.js`

**ai-teammate** (2026-10-04):
💡 **SUGGESTION: `rcRunIds` is dead code**

```js
var rcRunIds = [];
var rcSeen = {};
rcTargets.forEach(function (t) {
    if (rcSeen[t.runId]) return;
    rcSeen[t.runId] = true;
    rcRunIds.push(t.runId);
```

`rcRunIds` is populated and never read — `rcSeen` alone performs the per-run dedup (and the log line below re-derives the summary from `rcTargets`). Drop the array; less state to misread in an already guard-dense block.

---

### Thread 6 — `js/smAgent.js`

**ai-teammate** (2026-10-04):
💡 **SUGGESTION: both probes cap at `per_page=50` — busy heads can silently exceed the window**

`headWorkflowRuns` (this line) and the per-run jobs probe (line 2774) stop at 50. A long-lived PR head accumulates runs on every push × workflow (the gh-682 evidence alone shows 8+ kicker runs in one 36-second wave), and `actions/runs?head_sha=` returns newest-first — so on a sufficiently busy head the cancelled run can fall outside the first page. ---

### Thread 7 — `sm_github.json`

**ai-teammate** (2026-10-04):
💡 **SUGGESTION: `limit: 1` drains a cancel-wave one PR per 10-min tick**

The action itself is cheap (a few API reads + an idempotent `gh run rerun` — no workflow dispatch, no budget competition), but the gh-682 evidence shows eight branches' kickers cancelled inside one 36-second wave. At `limit: 1` on the 10-minute SM cadence that wave needs ~80 minutes to drain, with `ai_validated` queue-heads stuck BLOCKED the whole time — the dead-zone cost this PR is trying to eliminate. The sibling bulk rules use `limit: 10` (`sweep-stale-validating`, `silent-update-behind`); consider matching them, the guards (marker, in-flight probe, attempt-1-only) already bound the write side.

# Pull Request Information

- **PR #**: 695
- **URL**: https://github.com/IstiN/dmtools-agents/pull/695
- **Title**: gh-682: standing SM remedy — cancelled required checks re-run themselves (kicker cancel-loop)
- **Author**: IstiN
- **Branch**: `fix/682-rerun-cancelled-checks` → `main`
- **State**: open
- **Files Changed**: 4
- **Additions**: +617
- **Deletions**: -1
- **Created**: 2026-10-04T06:56:26Z
- **Updated**: 2026-10-04T07:54:58Z

## PR Description

Closes #682 (PR 1 of 2 — the kicker-side fix lands in IstiN/dmtools-agentic-workflows; this PR is the standing SM remedy + this repo's own stub scoping).

## Evidence (#682)

- **fa#1202** (head `898efd4`): all 4 kicker push-runs on `ai/gh-1171` CANCELLED 21:43–23:05 as silent-refresh pushes landed; required checks ended CANCELLED → PR BLOCKED until the manual rerun at 23:26.
- **fa#1203**: same pattern twice (23:47, 23:57) — the queue head stalled on it.
- **Still reproducing 2026-10-04 06:21–06:22**: eight branches' kicker runs cancelled inside one 36-second dev-wave (fa run ids 37182568709…37182598010); this repo's own kicker showed the same at 06:36/06:41/06:43.
- Cost on 2026-10-03 alone: 2 dead zones on queue heads + 2 manual reruns.

Mechanism: a queued run in a shared concurrency group **always supersedes the pending one** — *"Any existing pending job or workflow in the same concurrency group, if it exists, will be canceled and the new queued job or workflow will take its place"* (GitHub docs). `cancel-in-progress: false` only shields the RUNNING run. Every silent-refresh push therefore killed the pending kicker, and no rule treated CANCELLED as re-runnable (the #632 class, now triggered by our own refresh machinery).

## What this PR does

**1. Standing rule `rerun-cancelled-checks`** (`sm_github.json`, FIRST in the array):

- match: armed (`ai_validating`) or latched (`ai_validated`) PR; not BEHIND (silent-update refreshes that head), not DIRTY (conflict-rework owns it), not `agent:rework`;
- `localAction rerun_cancelled_checks` (js/smAgent.js):
  - scans the head's check runs — only contexts that currently read **CANCELLED** among `rule.requiredContexts` act (dart: `static`/`gate`/`agents-gate`; fa: the kicker's `kicker / sm-liveness`, `kicker / head-completeness`). Failure paths untouched — red stays `fail_validation` territory;
  - once-per-head marker comment (conflict_rework pacing) citing fa#1202/#1203 + 2026-10-04 06:21, posted AFTER the reruns land (the gh-683 bug C invariant: a failed rerun posts no marker, the next tick retries);
  - **no in-flight run on the head** guard — the `hasActiveDispatchedRun` probe pattern widened to every run on the head (any event): an active run re-stamps the contexts by itself;
  - `gh run rerun <id>` of the latest **attempt-1** cancelled run per required context (deduped per run id); a run already re-run and still cancelled is skipped — no automatic retry loop.
- Placement: it never touches labels and never dispatches workflows, so it **cannot fight `sweep-stale-validating`** (cancelled conclusions never sweep by design anyway); the documented #637 invariant (merge-validated before sweep) is preserved by prefixing, never interleaving.

**2. This repo's own kicker stub** (`.github/workflows/factory-sm-kicker.yml`): the caller-level global `sm-kicker` group alone would keep superseding pending kickers even after the canonical awf fix is re-pinned — scoped to `sm-kicker-${{ github.sha }}` (effective once the pin bump lands; pin bumps are separate PRs by repo convention).

## Tests

10 new unit tests in the existing `test_smAgent.js` rule-test patterns (rerun+marker shape, rerun-failure posts no marker, CANCELLED-only matching, in-flight skip, once-per-head pacing, attempt-2 no-loop, newest-run-wins, dry-run, no-config skip, and a `sm_github.json` placement pin asserting rule order). Node harness: 178 passed, 1 failed — the single failure is the pre-existing `assert.doesNotThrow` mock gap present on clean `main` (the canonical gate is the pack-release test job). `actionlint` clean. #684/#685/#686 suites untouched and green.

# PR Discussion History

_Previous review discussions for PR #695._

## Review Threads (Inline Comments)

### Thread 1 — `js/smAgent.js`

**ai-teammate** (2026-10-04):
🚨 **BLOCKING: the scan flags a required context as CANCELLED even when a NEWER run already re-stamped it green**

`cancelledRequiredContexts` treats the context as cancelled if **any** check run in the commit's rollup reads `CANCELLED`:

```js
rollup.forEach(function (r) {
    var name = r && (r.name || r.context);
    var concl = r && r.conclusion ? String(r.conclusion).toUpperCase() : null;
    if (name && concl === 'CANCELLED' && contexts.indexOf(name) !== -1) {
        cancelled[name] = true;
    }
});
```

`github_get_commit_check_runs` returns **all** check runs on the commit (verified live: "Get all check runs ... for a commit SHA") — including stale ones from earlier attempts/dispatches. Branch protection resolves each required context by its **latest** check run; this code does not, despite the comment claiming "the check-runs rollup is the source of truth".

Reachable sequence with this repo's own machinery:

1. Validation run A (attempt 1) on head H is cancelled — exactly the #632/#682 class this rule targets (or stale-run cleanup).
2. `revalidate-armed` re-dispatches a fresh run B on H after the 15-min grace → B re-stamps `static`/`gate`/`agents-gate` **green**.
3. Next tick this rule runs **first** (before `merge-validated`), sees A's stale `CANCELLED` check runs, and `gh run rerun`s A + posts the marker — on a head that is already green and mergeable.

Consequences: the merge is delayed a full validation cycle; if the spurious rerun fails (moved base, flake), the freshly re-stamped red hands the PR to `fail_validation` and it gets parked — the rule actively harms the PRs it protects. Same trap after the rule's own remedy: attempt-1 cancelled check runs persist next to attempt-2's, so any tick where the marker read errors (`catch` → `rcReported = false`) re-fires.

Fix (~5 lines): keep only the **latest** check run per required context (max `completed_at`, tie-break by `id`) before testing `=== 'CANCELLED'`, and add a test fixture with a stale-cancelled + fresh-green pair (the current fixtures only ever carry the cancelled runs, which pins the bug).

---

### Thread 2 — `js/smAgent.js`

**ai-teammate** (2026-10-04):
⚠️ **IMPORTANT: once-per-head marker is posted even when the rerun set covers only part of the cancelled contexts**

`rcTargets` can legitimately cover a **subset** of `rcCancelled`: contexts whose cancelled runs are already attempt-2+ (skipped by design), or whose job names don't match any walked run (`jobs?per_page=50` cap, job-name/context drift). The marker is then posted anyway, and from the next tick on the `rcReported` check short-circuits **before** the mapping probe — the head is "remedied" forever while the uncovered contexts still read `CANCELLED` (the exact gh-682 BLOCKED symptom), and even the per-tick `"no rerunnable ... skip"` warn disappears into the marker.

```js
if (rcReported) {
    console.log('  ⏭️  ' + key + ' cancelled checks already re-run for head — waiting on the rerun');
    continue;
}
```

Suggestion: post the marker only when `rcTargets` covers **all** of `rcCancelled` (or list the uncovered contexts in the marker text), so an unmapped context keeps visibly retrying/warning instead of being silently latched shut by a partial remediation. Test to add: two cancelled contexts where only one maps to an attempt-1 run → no marker on that tick.

---

### Thread 3 — `js/unit-tests/test_smAgent.js`

**ai-teammate** (2026-10-04):
⚠️ **IMPORTANT: copy-paste bug in the new test helper — `it[k] = extra` drops the `[k]` index**

```js
function prItem682(n, extra) {
    var it = { key: 'pr-' + n, labels: ['ai_validating'], issueNumber: null,
               prNumber: n, draft: false, branch: 'ai/gh-1202',
               pr: { headSha: '898efd4' } };
    if (extra) { for (var k in extra) { if (extra.hasOwnProperty(k)) it[k] = extra; } }
    return it;
}
```

Every sibling helper in this file does `it[k] = extra[k]` (lines 855, 1682, 1864, 2041) — this copy assigns the whole `extra` object to every key. It is latent today only because every call site is `prItem682(1202)`; the first caller that passes `extra` (e.g. `prItem682(1202, { labels: ['ai_validated'] })`) gets `{ labels: {labels: [...]}, prNumber: {labels: [...]}, ... }` and a silently wrong fixture. One-character fix.

---

### Thread 4 — `js/smAgent.js`

**ai-teammate** (2026-10-04):
💡 **SUGGESTION: `number:` vs `pullRequestId:` — keep one spelling per tool in this file**

This new call site passes `number: ticket.prNumber` to `github_get_pr_comments`, while all 8 other call sites in this file (1573, 1817, 1845, 1993, 2020, 2165, 2979 …) use `pullRequestId:`. Both aliases work against the current dmtools runtime (verified live), but if the tool ever tightens its input schema, every site should already agree — `pullRequestId` is the canonical name per `js/common/trackers.js` ("the number argument keeps the tool's canonical pullRequestId name"). Same payload, just match the file's existing contract.

---

### Thread 5 — `js/smAgent.js`

**ai-teammate** (2026-10-04):
💡 **SUGGESTION: `rcRunIds` is dead code**

```js
var rcRunIds = [];
var rcSeen = {};
rcTargets.forEach(function (t) {
    if (rcSeen[t.runId]) return;
    rcSeen[t.runId] = true;
    rcRunIds.push(t.runId);
```

`rcRunIds` is populated and never read — `rcSeen` alone performs the per-run dedup (and the log line below re-derives the summary from `rcTargets`). Drop the array; less state to misread in an already guard-dense block.

---

### Thread 6 — `js/smAgent.js`

**ai-teammate** (2026-10-04):
💡 **SUGGESTION: both probes cap at `per_page=50` — busy heads can silently exceed the window**

`headWorkflowRuns` (this line) and the per-run jobs probe (line 2774) stop at 50. A long-lived PR head accumulates runs on every push × workflow (the gh-682 evidence alone shows 8+ kicker runs in one 36-second wave), and `actions/runs?head_sha=` returns newest-first — so on a sufficiently busy head the cancelled run can fall outside the first page. Failure mode is quiet: the context still reads `CANCELLED` via the check-runs endpoint, but `rerunTargetsForCancelledContexts` finds no run → `⚠️ ... no rerunnable (attempt-1) cancelled run — skip, retry next tick` forever (no remedy, no marker). Either raise/page the cap for this targeted probe (a filtered `runs?head_sha=` + `conclusion=cancelled` server-side would shrink the payload too), or log the total_count when the window is saturated so the gap is visible.

---

### Thread 7 — `sm_github.json`

**ai-teammate** (2026-10-04):
💡 **SUGGESTION: `limit: 1` drains a cancel-wave one PR per 10-min tick**

The action itself is cheap (a few API reads + an idempotent `gh run rerun` — no workflow dispatch, no budget competition), but the gh-682 evidence shows eight branches' kickers cancelled inside one 36-second wave. At `limit: 1` on the 10-minute SM cadence that wave needs ~80 minutes to drain, with `ai_validated` queue-heads stuck BLOCKED the whole time — the dead-zone cost this PR is trying to eliminate. The sibling bulk rules use `limit: 10` (`sweep-stale-validating`, `silent-update-behind`); consider matching them, the guards (marker, in-flight probe, attempt-1-only) already bound the write side.

4. **The marker read: `github_get_pr_comments` pagination** — same pattern as conflict_rework pacing? Let me check how conflict_rework does its marker read to confirm consistency. If conflict_rework also reads comments via the same tool without pagination handling, consistent. Let me check line 1813-1845 (the headSha/marker reading in conflict_rework).

5. **DRY mode + `hasActiveHeadRun`**: In DRY, probes still execute gh commands via cli_execute_command — in dry-run the SM presumably shouldn't run side-effect commands, but gh api reads are fine, and `[dry]` logs. The `DRY` check only guards rerun+comment. Consistent with other actions? Probably. OK.

6. **`workflowBudget`**: the new rule doesn't consume workflowBudget — fine since it doesn't dispatch.

7. **Test fixture `commitCheckRuns` mock**: `smMocks.github_get_commit_check_runs` returns `opts.github.commitCheckRuns || { check_runs: [] }`. OK.

8. **`limit: 1` semantics**: `effectiveLimit` per rule. OK.

9. **Marker text says "a pending run superseded by the silent-refresh push wave"** — but the rule can also fire on cancels NOT caused by the refresh wave (any cancel). Cosmetic.

10. **The `rcReported` check runs BEFORE `hasActiveHeadRun`** — order: cancelled-scan → marker-read → in-flight probe → mapping. If a rerun is in flight (attempt 2 running), contexts may already read success (new attempt re-stamps immediately? no — attempt 2 check runs are created when the rerun starts; they'd read in-progress/pending, not cancelled). Then rcCancelled=[] → skip anyway. OK.

11. **New: what if the SAME head has marker from THIS rule AND then the base moves (BEHIND) → silent-update pushes new head → new head's kicker cancelled → rule acts on new head: marker contains new head sha → acts. Good (per-head keying works).

12. **`rcSeen`/`rcRunIds`** — dead code (previous #5).

13. **Concurrent same-run rerun dedup across ticks**: tick N: reruns run 555001 (attempt→2). Tick N+1: contexts read... attempt-2 in progress → check runs for the required context: the rerun creates new check runs in progress; the old cancelled attempt-1 check runs persist. `cancelledRequiredContexts` still sees attempt-1 CANCELLED → rcCancelled non-empty. Marker exists → rcReported → skip. Good. But if marker read FAILED (catch → rcReported=false): → hasActiveHeadRun: attempt-2 run is in_progress → skip. Good. If attempt-2 completed success: contexts read success (new check runs) but also cancelled (old) → rcCancelled non-empty (THE BUG #1); marker exists → skip (suppressed). If marker read failed AND attempt-2 succeeded: rcReported=false, hasActiveHeadRun=false, rcTargets: attempt-1 cancelled run now has run_attempt... wait — after rerun, does run 555001's run_attempt become 2? Yes — the run object's run_attempt increments to 2 on rerun. So `rerunTargetsForCancelledContexts` skips it (attempt>1) → no targets → warn "no rerunnable" → skip. Self-healing. OK — so the attempt-1 filter is a decent second line of defense for loops. Good design acknowledgment.

14. **Workflow file**: check the YAML diff again. The concurrency group change + comment. Any YAML validity issue? actionlint clean per PR. Let me verify YAML parses. Also confirm the `concurrency` placement (workflow-level). Also `github.sha` on `workflow_run`-triggered? The kicker triggers on `push` presumably. For `schedule` triggers github.sha = latest commit on default branch — fine.

Actually wait — one thing to check in the kicker workflow: if it has `schedule` triggers too, per-SHA grouping means scheduled kickers on the same SHA (default branch head) would queue behind each other (cancel-in-progress: false) — multiple scheduled ticks of the same SHA stack up rather than supersede. With a 10-min SM cadence and a global default-branch head SHA, several scheduled kickers could queue on the same SHA (if no new push happened, the SHA is stable) — they'd pile up: run 1 executes, runs 2..N execute serially, each dispatching a tick → repeated ticks? That's a behavior change: previously the global group with cancel-in-progress:false also queued pending runs (pending superseded pending). Hmm — actually under the OLD config, a new scheduled kicker (pending) superseded the pending ones, so at most 1-2 ran. Under the NEW per-SHA group, pending runs queue but do NOT supersede (different group per SHA → parallel; same group per SHA → queue, no cancel). Multiple queued runs in the same group all eventually run. So on the default branch with no pushes between scheduled ticks, every tick's kicker runs serially → N ticks dispatched in a burst. Is that harmful? The kicker presumably dispatches the SM (kicker / sm-liveness). Multiple rapid SM ticks = redundant but bounded by schedule frequency (10 min each). Mildly wasteful, not harmful — the SM itself has idempotent tick behavior. Actually wait — for the default branch, is the kicker even needed per-SHA? The schedule fires per workflow file, not per SHA... scheduled runs in the same concurrency group: with per-SHA group and cancel-in-progress:false, if two scheduled events fire while one runs, the pending ones queue (old behavior: newest supersedes pending → only 1 runs). New behavior: ALL of them run serially. Each run = one SM tick. Extra ticks are harmless-ish (SM ticks are idempotent, rate-limited by GitHub API), but on a quiet repo the schedule is presumably every ~5-10 min, and runs take ~1 min, so queueing is rare.

Hmm, but actually there's a subtler issue: for PUSH-triggered kicks on the default branch itself (factory-data snapshots push etc.), per-SHA means each push gets its own kicker — that's exactly the fix intent (no cross-branch superseding). The scheduling edge is minor. I'll mention as SUGGESTION? The previous review didn't flag it. It's a genuinely observable behavior change but benign. I could add it as a 💡. Let me check the workflow triggers first.

Let me read the full kicker workflow file.

# SM kicker — thin stub over the canonical watchdog in the factory home.
# All logic (sm-liveness + head-completeness) lives in
# IstiN/dmtools-agentic-workflows/.github/workflows/factory-sm-kicker.yml.
# This repo's validation CI is `Quality` (display name "Quality") and its
# required context is the `crap` job.
name: SM kicker

run-name: '🥁 kicker ${{ github.event_name }} ${{ github.ref_name }}'

on:
  push:
    branches-ignore: [main]
  schedule:
    - cron: '13,43 * * * *'
  workflow_dispatch:

permissions:
  actions: write
  contents: read
  pull-requests: read
  checks: read

concurrency:
  # dmtools-agents#682 (live fa#1202/#1203 2026-10-03, still reproducing
  # 2026-10-04 06:21–06:22 in THIS repo — runs 06:36/06:41/06:43): the
  # global group below already ran with cancel-in-progress:false, yet
  # kicker runs kept dying cancelled in chains. cancel-in-progress only
  # shields the RUNNING run — a queued run in the same group ALWAYS
  # supersedes (cancels) the pending one (GitHub docs: "Any existing
  # pending job or workflow in the same concurrency group, if it exists,
  # will be canceled and the new queued job or workflow will take its
  # place"). One global group meant every push anywhere (silent refresh,
  # factory-data snapshots, dev waves) cancelled every other branch's
  # pending kicker. Per-head-SHA group: no push can displace another
  # push's kicker — a queued kicker that is about to dispatch a tick
  # always gets to run (canonical fix + consumer notes: IstiN/
  # dmtools-agentic-workflows factory-sm-kicker.yml). Effective once the
  # canonical pin is bumped (separate PR): until then the called
  # workflow's own global group still supersedes.
  group: sm-kicker-${{ github.sha }}
  cancel-in-progress: false

jobs:
  kicker:
    uses: IstiN/dmtools-agentic-workflows/.github/workflows/factory-sm-kicker.yml@6e8e40eae1cd0f64bedef166b7b6eb92c76c8485
    with:
      sm_workflow: machine-sm.yml
      ci_workflow: quality.yml
      ci_display_name: Quality
      required_contexts: crap

Read ticket files to understand WHY it changed and verify against requirements. ## 2. Diff checklist — apply to `pr_diff.txt` For every hunk, ask at least these questions: - [ ] Does the change match the ticket scope? Any scope creep? - [ ] Are new or changed public APIs contract-safe for existing callers? - [ ] Is user/external input validated, sanitized, or escaped? - [ ] Are secrets, tokens, or PATs handled safely — not logged, not interpolated into shell scripts? - [ ] Are new or modified files present under `testing/` in a non-test-automation PR? - [ ] Is dead code, unused imports, or obvious duplication introduced? - [ ] Are error paths handled, or are failures silently swallowed? - [ ] Are new dependencies justified and compatible with the existing stack? - [ ] Beyond blockers: what other maintainability, correctness, or quality improvements are visible in the changed code? ## 3. Changed-file deep read Do not review from the diff alone. Read the full content of every changed file: - imports and dependencies - class/method responsibilities and adherence to SRP / OOP principles - naming consistency with the rest of the codebase - error handling, logging, and edge cases - test coverage for changed behavior - backward-compatibility and migration impact ## 4. Severity classification Classify every finding before writing outputs: - **BLOCKING** — merge would cause a bug, security issue, data loss, or CI break. Must be fixed. - **IMPORTANT** — real maintainability or correctness issue. Strongly prefer fixing before merge. - **SUGGESTION** — optional improvement, style, or future polish. Does not block merge. When in doubt, start one level higher; downgrade only after confirming the risk is negligible. ## 7. Exhaustive single-pass review Treat **every** review as the final and only review pass. The author will not get another chance to catch missed findings cheaply. - Do not defer SUGGESTION or IMPORTANT items to a later round because a BLOCKING issue exists. - After classifying all findings, re-read every changed file and ask: *"What else is improvable here?"* - Before writing outputs, verify that no obvious quality, maintainability, or correctness issue was left unreported. - Aim to surface the maximum number of actionable findings in this single iteration. ## 8. Outputs Write the standard review artifacts: - `outputs/pr_review.json` — structured data with `recommendation`, `summary`, `inlineComments`, `issueCounts` - `outputs/pr_review_general.md` — 1-2 paragraph general PR comment - `outputs/pr_review_comments/*.md` — one file per detailed inline comment **Inline comment lines must be present in the PR diff.** GitHub review threads can only be attached to added or context lines inside a diff hunk. # Pull Request Information

- **PR #**: 695
- **URL**: https://github.com/IstiN/dmtools-agents/pull/695
- **Title**: gh-682: standing SM remedy — cancelled required checks re-run themselves (kicker cancel-loop)
- **Author**: IstiN
- **Branch**: `fix/682-rerun-cancelled-checks` → `main`
- **State**: open
- **Files Changed**: 4
- **Additions**: +617
- **Deletions**: -1
- **Created**: 2026-10-04T06:56:26Z
- **Updated**: 2026-10-04T07:54:58Z

## PR Description

Closes #682 (PR 1 of 2 — the kicker-side fix lands in IstiN/dmtools-agentic-workflows; this PR is the standing SM remedy + this repo's own stub scoping).

## Evidence (#682)

- **fa#1202** (head `898efd4`): all 4 kicker push-runs on `ai/gh-1171` CANCELLED 21:43–23:05 as silent-refresh pushes landed; required checks ended CANCELLED → PR BLOCKED until the manual rerun at 23:26.
- **fa#1203**: same pattern twice (23:47, 23:57) — the queue head stalled on it.
- **Still reproducing 2026-10-04 06:21–06:22**: eight branches' kicker runs cancelled inside one 36-second dev-wave (fa run ids 37182568709…37182598010); this repo's own kicker showed the same at 06:36/06:41/06:43.
- Cost on 2026-10-03 alone: 2 dead zones on queue heads + 2 manual reruns.

Mechanism: a queued run in a shared concurrency group **always supersedes the pending one** — *"Any existing pending job or workflow in the same concurrency group, if it exists, will be canceled and the new queued job or workflow will take its place"* (GitHub docs). `cancel-in-progress: false` only shields the RUNNING run. Every silent-refresh push therefore killed the pending kicker, and no rule treated CANCELLED as re-runnable (the #632 class, now triggered by our own refresh machinery).

## What this PR does

**1. Standing rule `rerun-cancelled-checks`** (`sm_github.json`, FIRST in the array):

- match: armed (`ai_validating`) or latched (`ai_validated`) PR; not BEHIND (silent-update refreshes that head), not DIRTY (conflict-rework owns it), not `agent:rework`;
- `localAction rerun_cancelled_checks` (js/smAgent.js):
  - scans the head's check runs — only contexts that currently read **CANCELLED** among `rule.requiredContexts` act (dart: `static`/`gate`/`agents-gate`; fa: the kicker's `kicker / sm-liveness`, `kicker / head-completeness`). Failure paths untouched — red stays `fail_validation` territory;
  - once-per-head marker comment (conflict_rework pacing) citing fa#1202/#1203 + 2026-10-04 06:21, posted AFTER the reruns land (the gh-683 bug C invariant: a failed rerun posts no marker, the next tick retries);
  - **no in-flight run on the head** guard — the `hasActiveDispatchedRun` probe pattern widened to every run on the head (any event): an active run re-stamps the contexts by itself;
  - `gh run rerun <id>` of the latest **attempt-1** cancelled run per required context (deduped per run id); a run already re-run and still cancelled is skipped — no automatic retry loop.
- Placement: it never touches labels and never dispatches workflows, so it **cannot fight `sweep-stale-validating`** (cancelled conclusions never sweep by design anyway); the documented #637 invariant (merge-validated before sweep) is preserved by prefixing, never interleaving.

**2. This repo's own kicker stub** (`.github/workflows/factory-sm-kicker.yml`): the caller-level global `sm-kicker` group alone would keep superseding pending kickers even after the canonical awf fix is re-pinned — scoped to `sm-kicker-${{ github.sha }}` (effective once the pin bump lands; pin bumps are separate PRs by repo convention).

## Tests

10 new unit tests in the existing `test_smAgent.js` rule-test patterns (rerun+marker shape, rerun-failure posts no marker, CANCELLED-only matching, in-flight skip, once-per-head pacing, attempt-2 no-loop, newest-run-wins, dry-run, no-config skip, and a `sm_github.json` placement pin asserting rule order). Node harness: 178 passed, 1 failed — the single failure is the pre-existing `assert.doesNotThrow` mock gap present on clean `main` (the canonical gate is the pack-release test job). `actionlint` clean. #684/#685/#686 suites untouched and green.

# PR Discussion History

_Previous review discussions for PR #695._

## Review Threads (Inline Comments)

### Thread 1 — `js/smAgent.js`

**ai-teammate** (2026-10-04):
🚨 **BLOCKING: the scan flags a required context as CANCELLED even when a NEWER run already re-stamped it green**

`cancelledRequiredContexts` treats the context as cancelled if **any** check run in the commit's rollup reads `CANCELLED`:

```js
rollup.forEach(function (r) {
    var name = r && (r.name || r.context);
    var concl = r && r.conclusion ? String(r.conclusion).toUpperCase() : null;
    if (name && concl === 'CANCELLED' && contexts.indexOf(name) !== -1) {
        cancelled[name] = true;
    }
});
```

`github_get_commit_check_runs` returns **all** check runs on the commit (verified live: "Get all check runs ... for a commit SHA") — including stale ones from earlier attempts/dispatches. Branch protection resolves each required context by its **latest** check run; this code does not, despite the comment claiming "the check-runs rollup is the source of truth".

Reachable sequence with this repo's own machinery:

1. Validation run A (attempt 1) on head H is cancelled — exactly the #632/#682 class this rule targets (or stale-run cleanup).
2. `revalidate-armed` re-dispatches a fresh run B on H after the 15-min grace → B re-stamps `static`/`gate`/`agents-gate` **green**.
3. Next tick this rule runs **first** (before `merge-validated`), sees A's stale `CANCELLED` check runs, and `gh run rerun`s A + posts the marker — on a head that is already green and mergeable.

Consequences: the merge is delayed a full validation cycle; if the spurious rerun fails (moved base, flake), the freshly re-stamped red hands the PR to `fail_validation` and it gets parked — the rule actively harms the PRs it protects. Same trap after the rule's own remedy: attempt-1 cancelled check runs persist next to attempt-2's, so any tick where the marker read errors (`catch` → `rcReported = false`) re-fires.

Fix (~5 lines): keep only the **latest** check run per required context (max `completed_at`, tie-break by `id`) before testing `=== 'CANCELLED'`, and add a test fixture with a stale-cancelled + fresh-green pair (the current fixtures only ever carry the cancelled runs, which pins the bug).

---

### Thread 2 — `js/smAgent.js`

**ai-teammate** (2026-10-04):
⚠️ **IMPORTANT: once-per-head marker is posted even when the rerun set covers only part of the cancelled contexts**

`rcTargets` can legitimately cover a **subset** of `rcCancelled`: contexts whose cancelled runs are already attempt-2+ (skipped by design), or whose job names don't match any walked run (`jobs?per_page=50` cap, job-name/context drift). The marker is then posted anyway, and from the next tick on the `rcReported` check short-circuits **before** the mapping probe — the head is "remedied" forever while the uncovered contexts still read `CANCELLED` (the exact gh-682 BLOCKED symptom), and even the per-tick `"no rerunnable ... skip"` warn disappears into the marker.

```js
if (rcReported) {
    console.log('  ⏭️  ' + key + ' cancelled checks already re-run for head — waiting on the rerun');
    continue;
}
```

Suggestion: post the marker only when `rcTargets` covers **all** of `rcCancelled` (or list the uncovered contexts in the marker text), so an unmapped context keeps visibly retrying/warning instead of being silently latched shut by a partial remediation. Test to add: two cancelled contexts where only one maps to an attempt-1 run → no marker on that tick.

---

### Thread 3 — `js/unit-tests/test_smAgent.js`

**ai-teammate** (2026-10-04):
⚠️ **IMPORTANT: copy-paste bug in the new test helper — `it[k] = extra` drops the `[k]` index**

```js
function prItem682(n, extra) {
```

# Pull Request Information

- **PR #**: 695
- **URL**: https://github.com/IstiN/dmtools-agents/pull/695
- **Title**: gh-682: standing SM remedy — cancelled required checks re-run themselves (kicker cancel-loop)
- **Author**: IstiN
- **Branch**: `fix/682-rerun-cancelled-checks` → `main`
- **State**: open
- **Files Changed**: 4
- **Additions**: +617
- **Deletions**: -1
- **Created**: 2026-10-04T06:56:26Z
- **Updated**: 2026-10-04T07:54:58Z

## PR Description

Closes #682 (PR 1 of 2 — the kicker-side fix lands in IstiN/dmtools-agentic-workflows; this PR is the standing SM remedy + this repo's own stub scoping).

## Evidence (#682)

- **fa#1202** (head `898efd4`): all 4 kicker push-runs on `ai/gh-1171` CANCELLED 21:43–23:05 as silent-refresh pushes landed; required checks ended CANCELLED → PR BLOCKED until the manual rerun at 23:26.
- **fa#1203**: same pattern twice (23:47, 23:57) — the queue head stalled on it.
- **Still reproducing 2026-10-04 06:21–06:22**: eight branches' kicker runs cancelled inside one 36-second dev-wave (fa run ids 37182568709…37182598010); this repo's own kicker showed the same at 06:36/06:41/06:43.
- Cost on 2026-10-03 alone: 2 dead zones on queue heads + 2 manual reruns.

Mechanism: a queued run in a shared concurrency group **always supersedes the pending one** — *"Any existing pending job or workflow in the same concurrency group, if it exists, will be canceled and the new queued job or workflow will take its place"* (GitHub docs). `cancel-in-progress: false` only shields the RUNNING run. Every silent-refresh push therefore killed the pending kicker, and no rule treated CANCELLED as re-runnable (the #632 class, now triggered by our own refresh machinery).

## What this PR does

**1. Standing rule `rerun-cancelled-checks`** (`sm_github.json`, FIRST in the array):

- match: armed (`ai_validating`) or latched (`ai_validated`) PR; not BEHIND (silent-update refreshes that head), not DIRTY (conflict-rework owns it), not `agent:rework`;
- `localAction rerun_cancelled_checks` (js/smAgent.js):
  - scans the head's check runs — only contexts that currently read **CANCELLED** among `rule.requiredContexts` act (dart: `static`/`gate`/`agents-gate`; fa: the kicker's `kicker / sm-liveness`, `kicker / head-completeness`). Failure paths untouched — red stays `fail_validation` territory;
  - once-per-head marker comment (conflict_rework pacing) citing fa#1202/#1203 + 2026-10-04 06:21, posted AFTER the reruns land (the gh-683 bug C invariant: a failed rerun posts no marker, the next tick retries);
  - **no in-flight run on the head** guard — the `hasActiveDispatchedRun` probe pattern widened to every run on the head (any event): an active run re-stamps the contexts by itself;
  - `gh run rerun <id>` of the latest **attempt-1** cancelled run per required context (deduped per run id); a run already re-run and still cancelled is skipped — no automatic retry loop.
- Placement: it never touches labels and never dispatches workflows, so it **cannot fight `sweep-stale-validating`** (cancelled conclusions never sweep by design anyway); the documented #637 invariant (merge-validated before sweep) is preserved by prefixing, never interleaving.

**2. This repo's own kicker stub** (`.github/workflows/factory-sm-kicker.yml`): the caller-level global `sm-kicker` group alone would keep superseding pending kickers even after the canonical awf fix is re-pinned — scoped to `sm-kicker-${{ github.sha }}` (effective once the pin bump lands; pin bumps are separate PRs by repo convention).

## Tests

10 new unit tests in the existing `test_smAgent.js` rule-test patterns (rerun+marker shape, rerun-failure posts no marker, CANCELLED-only matching, in-flight skip, once-per-head pacing, attempt-2 no-loop, newest-run-wins, dry-run, no-config skip, and a `sm_github.json` placement pin asserting rule order). Node harness: 178 passed, 1 failed — the single failure is the pre-existing `assert.doesNotThrow` mock gap present on clean `main` (the canonical gate is the pack-release test job). `actionlint` clean. #684/#685/#686 suites untouched and green.

- match: armed (`ai_validating`) or latched (`ai_validated`) PR; not BEHIND (silent-update refreshes that head), not DIRTY (conflict-rework owns it), not `agent:rework`;
- `localAction rerun_cancelled_checks` (js/smAgent.js):
  - scans the head's check runs — only contexts that currently read **CANCELLED** among `rule.requiredContexts` act (dart: `static`/`gate`/`agents-gate`; fa: the kicker's `kicker / sm-liveness`, `kicker / head-completeness`). Failure paths untouched — red stays `fail_validation` territory;
  - once-per-head marker comment (conflict_rework pacing) citing fa#1202/#1203 + 2026-10-04 06:21, posted AFTER the reruns land (the gh-683 bug C invariant: a failed rerun posts no marker, the next tick retries);
  - **no in-flight run on the head** guard — the `hasActiveDispatchedRun` probe pattern widened to every run on the head (any event): an active run re-stamps the contexts by itself;
  - `gh run rerun <id>` of the latest **attempt-1** cancelled run per required context (deduped per run id); a run already re-run and still cancelled is skipped — no automatic retry loop.
- Placement: it never touches labels and never dispatches workflows, so it **cannot fight `sweep-stale-validating`** (cancelled conclusions never sweep by design anyway); the documented #637 invariant (merge-validated before sweep) is preserved by prefixing, never interleaving.

**2. This repo's own kicker stub** (`.github/workflows/factory-sm-kicker.yml`): the caller-level global `sm-kicker` group alone would keep superseding pending kickers even after the canonical awf fix is re-pinned — scoped to `sm-kicker-${{ github.sha }}` (effective once the pin bump lands; pin bumps are separate PRs by repo convention).

## Tests

10 new unit tests in the existing `test_smAgent.js` rule-test patterns (rerun+marker shape, rerun-failure posts no marker, CANCELLED-only matching, in-flight skip, once-per-head pacing, attempt-2 no-loop, newest-run-wins, dry-run, no-config skip, and a `sm_github.json` placement pin asserting rule order). Node harness: 178 passed, 1 failed — the single failure is the pre-existing `assert.doesNotThrow` mock gap present on clean `main` (the canonical gate is the pack-release test job). `actionlint` clean. #684/#685/#686 suites untouched and green.

# PR Discussion History

_Previous review discussions for PR #695._

## Review Threads (Inline Comments)

### Thread 1 — `js/smAgent.js`

**ai-teammate** (2026-10-04):
🚨 **BLOCKING: the scan flags a required context as CANCELLED even when a NEWER run already re-stamped it green**

`cancelledRequiredContexts` treats the context as cancelled if **any** check run in the commit's rollup reads `CANCELLED`:

```js
rollup.forEach(function (r) {
    var name = r && (r.name || r.context);
    var concl = r && r.conclusion ? String(r.conclusion).toUpperCase() : null;
    if (name && concl === 'CANCELLED' && contexts.indexOf(name) !== -1) {
        cancelled[name] = true;
    }
});
```

`github_get_commit_check_runs` returns **all** check runs on the commit (verified live: "Get all check runs ... for a commit SHA") — including stale ones from earlier attempts/dispatches. Branch protection resolves each required context by its **latest** check run; this code does not, despite the comment claiming "the check-runs rollup is the source of truth".

Reachable sequence with this repo's own machinery:

1. Validation run A (attempt 1) on head H is cancelled — exactly the #632/#682 class this rule targets (or stale-run cleanup).
2. `revalidate-armed` re-dispatches a fresh run B on H after the 15-min grace → B re-stamps `static`/`gate`/`agents-gate` **green**.
3. Next tick this rule runs **first** (before `merge-validated`), sees A's stale `CANCELLED` check runs, and `gh run rerun`s A + posts the marker — on a head that is already green and mergeable.

Consequences: the merge is delayed a full validation cycle; if the spurious rerun fails (moved base, flake), the freshly re-stamped red hands the PR to `fail_validation` and it gets parked — the rule actively harms the PRs it protects. Same trap after the rule's own remedy: attempt-1 cancelled check runs persist next to attempt-2's, so any tick where the marker read errors (`catch` → `rcReported = false`) re-fires.

Fix (~5 lines): keep only the **latest** check run per required context (max `completed_at`, tie-break by `id`) before testing `=== 'CANCELLED'`, and add a test fixture with a stale-cancelled + fresh-green pair (the current fixtures only ever carry the cancelled runs, which pins the bug).

---

### Thread 2 — `js/smAgent.js`

**ai-teammate** (2026-10-04):
⚠️ **IMPORTANT: once-per-head marker is posted even when the rerun set covers only part of the cancelled contexts**

`rcTargets` can legitimately cover a **subset** of `rcCancelled`: contexts whose cancelled runs are already attempt-2+ (skipped by design), or whose job names don't match any walked run (`jobs?per_page=50` cap, job-name/context drift). The marker is then posted anyway, and from the next tick on the `rcReported` check short-circuits **before** the mapping probe — the head is "remedied" forever while the uncovered contexts still read `CANCELLED` (the exact gh-682 BLOCKED symptom), and even the per-tick `"no rerunnable ... skip"` warn disappears into the marker.

```js
if (rcReported) {
    console.log('  ⏭️  ' + key + ' cancelled checks already re-run for head — waiting on the rerun');
    continue;
}
```

Suggestion: post the marker only when `rcTargets` covers **all** of `rcCancelled` (or list the uncovered contexts in the marker text), so an unmapped context keeps visibly retrying/warning instead of being silently latched shut by a partial remediation. Test to add: two cancelled contexts where only one maps to an attempt-1 run → no marker on that tick.

---

### Thread 3 — `js/unit-tests/test_smAgent.js`

**ai-teammate** (2026-10-04):
⚠️ **IMPORTANT: copy-paste bug in the new test helper — `it[k] = extra` drops the `[k]` index**

```js
function prItem682(n, extra) {
    var it = { key: 'pr-' + n, labels: ['ai_validating'], issueNumber: null,
               prNumber: n, draft: false, branch: 'ai/gh-1202',
               pr: { headSha: '898efd4' } };
    if (extra) { for (var k in extra) { if (extra.hasOwnProperty(k)) it[k] = extra; } }
    return it;
}
```

Every sibling helper in this file does `it[k] = extra[k]` (lines 855, 1682, 1864, 2041) — this copy assigns the whole `extra` object to every key. It is latent today only because every call site is `prItem682(1202)`; the first caller that passes `extra` (e.g. `prItem682(1202, { labels: ['ai_validated'] })`) gets `{ labels: {labels: [...]}, prNumber: {labels: [...]}, ... }` and a silently wrong fixture. One-character fix.

---

### Thread 4 — `js/smAgent.js`

**ai-teammate** (2026-10-04):
💡 **SUGGESTION: `number:` vs `pullRequestId:` — keep one spelling per tool in this file**

This new call site passes `number: ticket.prNumber` to `github_get_pr_comments`, while all 8 other call sites in this file (1573, 1817, 1845, 1993, 2020, 2165, 2979 …) use `pullRequestId:`. Both aliases work against the current dmtools runtime (verified live), but if the tool ever tightens its input schema, every site should already agree — `pullRequestId` is the canonical name per `js/common/trackers.js` ("the number argument keeps the tool's canonical pullRequestId name"). Same payload, just match the file's existing contract.

---

### Thread 5 — `js/smAgent.js`

**ai-teammate** (2026-10-04):
💡 **SUGGESTION: `rcRunIds` is dead code**

```js
var rcRunIds = [];
var rcSeen = {};
rcTargets.forEach(function (t) {
    if (rcSeen[t.runId]) return;
    rcSeen[t.runId] = true;
    rcRunIds.push(t.runId);
```

`rcRunIds` is populated and never read — `rcSeen` alone performs the per-run dedup (and the log line below re-derives the summary from `rcTargets`). Drop the array; less state to misread in an already guard-dense block.

---

### Thread 6 — `js/smAgent.js`

**ai-teammate** (2026-10-04):
💡 **SUGGESTION: both probes cap at `per_page=50` — busy heads can silently exceed the window**

`headWorkflowRuns` (this line) and the per-run jobs probe (line 2774) stop at 50. A long-lived PR head accumulates runs on every push × workflow (the gh-682 evidence alone shows 8+ kicker runs in one 36-second wave), and `actions/runs?head_sha=` returns newest-first — so on a sufficiently busy head the cancelled run can fall outside the first page. Failure mode is quiet: the context still reads `CANCELLED` via the check-runs endpoint, but `rerunTargetsForCancelledContexts` finds no run → `⚠️ ... no rerunnable (attempt-1) cancelled run — skip, retry next tick` forever (no remedy, no marker). Either raise/page the cap for this targeted probe (a filtered `runs?head_sha=` + `conclusion=cancelled` server-side would shrink the payload too), or log the total_count when the window is saturated so the gap is visible.

---

### Thread 7 — `sm_github.json`

**ai-teammate** (2026-10-04):
💡 **SUGGESTION: `limit: 1` drains a cancel-wave one PR per 10-min tick**

The action itself is cheap (a few API reads + an idempotent `gh run rerun` — no workflow dispatch, no budget competition), but the gh-682 evidence shows eight branches' kickers cancelled inside one 36-second wave. At `limit: 1` on the 10-minute SM cadence that wave needs ~80 minutes to drain, with `ai_validated` queue-heads stuck BLOCKED the whole time — the dead-zone cost this PR is trying to eliminate. The sibling bulk rules use `limit: 10` (`sweep-stale-validating`, `silent-update-behind`); consider matching them, the guards (marker, in-flight probe, attempt-1-only) already bound the write side.

**Key Issues**:
- 🚨 `js/smAgent.js:2733` — stale check-run matching; fix = latest-check-run-per-context before the `CANCELLED` test (+ fixture with stale-cancelled + fresh-green pair)

# required context is the `crap` job.
name: SM kicker

run-name: '🥁 kicker ${{ github.event_name }} ${{ github.ref_name }}'

on:
  push:
    branches-ignore: [main]
  schedule:
    - cron: '13,43 * * * *'
  workflow_dispatch:

permissions:
  actions: write
  contents: read
  pull-requests: read
  checks: read

concurrency:
  # dmtools-agents#682 (live fa#1202/#1203 2026-10-03, still reproducing
  # 2026-10-04 06:21–06:22 in THIS repo — runs 06:36/06:41/06:43): the
  # global group below already ran with cancel-in-progress:false, yet
  # kicker runs kept dying cancelled in chains. cancel-in-progress only
  # shields the RUNNING run — a queued run in the same group ALWAYS
  # supersedes (cancels) the pending one (GitHub docs: "Any existing
  # pending job or workflow in the same concurrency group, if it exists,
  # will be canceled and the new queued job or workflow will take its
  # place"). One global group meant every push anywhere (silent refresh,
  # factory-data snapshots, dev waves) cancelled every other branch's
  # pending kicker. Per-head-SHA group: no push can displace another
  # push's kicker — a queued kicker that is about to dispatch a tick
  # always gets to run (canonical fix + consumer notes: IstiN/
  # dmtools-agentic-workflows factory-sm-kicker.yml). Effective once the
  # canonical pin is bumped (separate PR): until then the called
  # workflow's own global group still supersedes.
  group: sm-kicker-${{ github.sha }}
  cancel-in-progress: false

jobs:
  kicker:
    uses: IstiN/dmtools-agentic-workflows/.github/workflows/factory-sm-kicker.yml@6e8e40eae1cd0f64bedef166b7b6eb92c76c8485
    with:
      sm_workflow: machine-sm.yml
      ci_workflow: quality.yml
      ci_display_name: Quality
      required_contexts: crap

Confirmed:
- conflict_rework uses `pullRequestId: ticket.prNumber` for `github_get_pr_comments` — the new code uses `number:` — previous SUGGESTION #4 stands (consistency).
- The kicker workflow has `schedule` (every 30 min: 13,43 *) and `push` (branches-ignore main) and `workflow_dispatch`. Per-SHA group: scheduled runs on the default branch (main) — github.sha for schedule = latest commit on main. If main is quiet, consecutive scheduled kickers share the same SHA → same group → they queue (cancel-in-progress:false) and ALL run serially. Previously: newest superseded pending → only newest ran. So on a quiet main, each scheduled tick now executes every 30 min anyway (13 and 43 = every 30 min, runs take <1 min) — queueing would only matter if a run takes >30 min, which it doesn't. Actually wait — 13,43 means twice an hour. Runs are minutes apart (30 min). No queueing risk. And on dev waves with pushes, each SHA gets its own kicker → the fix. The `workflow_dispatch` on the same SHA twice → queue, fine.

So the workflow change is sound. The schedule edge is negligible — not worth reporting? Per "exhaustive single pass" I could note it, but it must be actionable. Honestly it's a non-issue: 30-min cadence, sub-minute runs. Skip.

Now — one more check on the BLOCKING bug: I should verify my claim that `github_get_commit_check_runs` returns ALL check runs (including stale). Let me check how the tool is used elsewhere in the repo and what it returns. Search for github_get_commit_check_runs usage and any docs. Input context — MANDATORY reading order ```mermaid flowchart TD subgraph PR_CONTEXT["⚠️ PR-specific files (read first)"] P1["1️⃣ instruction.md (repo root) — project stack, conventions"] P2["2️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_info.md — PR title, author, branch, description"] P3["3️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_diff.txt — the diff to review"] P4["4️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_files.txt — list of changed files"] P5["5️⃣ input/TICKET/ci_failures.md — CI failures = BLOCKING (last 500 lines)"] P5_FULL["5️⃣ input/TICKET/ci_failures_full.log — full CI logs"] P6["6️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_discussions.md + pr_discussions_raw.json — existing comments"] P1 --> P2 --> P3 --> P4 --> P5 --> P5_FULL --> P6 end subgraph TICKET_CONTEXT["Ticket context (for understanding PR purpose)"] T1["7️⃣ input/TICKET/ticket.md — linked ticket description, ACs"] T2["8️⃣ input/TICKET/comments.md — ticket discussion if present"] T3["9️⃣ input/TICKET/parent-*.md — parent story context"] T4["🔟 input/TICKET/confluence/*.md — linked specifications"] T1 --> T2 --> T3 --> T4 end subgraph RULE["⚠️ Rule"] R1["If file exists in input/ → read locally, do NOT re-fetch via dmtools"] end PR_CONTEXT --> TICKET_CONTEXT --> RULE ``` Read PR files to understand WHAT changed. Read ticket files to understand WHY it changed and verify against requirements. ## 2. Diff checklist — apply to `pr_diff.txt` For every hunk, ask at least these questions: - [ ] Does the change match the ticket scope? Any scope creep? - [ ] Are new or changed public APIs contract-safe for existing callers? - [ ] Is user/external input validated, sanitized, or escaped? - [ ] Are secrets, tokens, or PATs handled safely — not logged, not interpolated into shell scripts? - [ ] Are new or modified files present under `testing/` in a non-test-automation PR? - [ ] Is dead code, unused imports, or obvious duplication introduced? - [ ] Are error paths handled, or are failures silently swallowed? - [ ] Are new dependencies justified and compatible with the existing stack? - [ ] Beyond blockers: what other maintainability, correctness, or quality improvements are visible in the changed code? ## 3. # Pull Request Information

- **PR #**: 695
- **URL**: https://github.com/IstiN/dmtools-agents/pull/695
- **Title**: gh-682: standing SM remedy — cancelled required checks re-run themselves (kicker cancel-loop)
- **Author**: IstiN
- **Branch**: `fix/682-rerun-cancelled-checks` → `main`
- **State**: open
- **Files Changed**: 4
- **Additions**: +617
- **Deletions**: -1
- **Created**: 2026-10-04T06:56:26Z
- **Updated**: 2026-10-04T07:54:58Z

## PR Description

Closes #682 (PR 1 of 2 — the kicker-side fix lands in IstiN/dmtools-agentic-workflows; this PR is the standing SM remedy + this repo's own stub scoping).

## Evidence (#682)

- **fa#1202** (head `898efd4`): all 4 kicker push-runs on `ai/gh-1171` CANCELLED 21:43–23:05 as silent-refresh pushes landed; required checks ended CANCELLED → PR BLOCKED until the manual rerun at 23:26.
- **fa#1203**: same pattern twice (23:47, 23:57) — the queue head stalled on it.
- **Still reproducing 2026-10-04 06:21–06:22**: eight branches' kicker runs cancelled inside one 36-second dev-wave (fa run ids 37182568709…37182598010); this repo's own kicker showed the same at 06:36/06:41/06:43.
- Cost on 2026-10-03 alone: 2 dead zones on queue heads + 2 manual reruns.

Mechanism: a queued run in a shared concurrency group **always supersedes the pending one** — *"Any existing pending job or workflow in the same concurrency group, if it exists, will be canceled and the new queued job or workflow will take its place"* (GitHub docs). `cancel-in-progress: false` only shields the RUNNING run. Every silent-refresh push therefore killed the pending kicker, and no rule treated CANCELLED as re-runnable (the #632 class, now triggered by our own refresh machinery).

## What this PR does

**1. Standing rule `rerun-cancelled-checks`** (`sm_github.json`, FIRST in the array):

- match: armed (`ai_validating`) or latched (`ai_validated`) PR; not BEHIND (silent-update refreshes that head), not DIRTY (conflict-rework owns it), not `agent:rework`;
- `localAction rerun_cancelled_checks` (js/smAgent.js):
  - scans the head's check runs — only contexts that currently read **CANCELLED** among `rule.requiredContexts` act (dart: `static`/`gate`/`agents-gate`; fa: the kicker's `kicker / sm-liveness`, `kicker / head-completeness`). Failure paths untouched — red stays `fail_validation` territory;
  - once-per-head marker comment (conflict_rework pacing) citing fa#1202/#1203 + 2026-10-04 06:21, posted AFTER the reruns land (the gh-683 bug C invariant: a failed rerun posts no marker, the next tick retries);
  - **no in-flight run on the head** guard — the `hasActiveDispatchedRun` probe pattern widened to every run on the head (any event): an active run re-stamps the contexts by itself;
  - `gh run rerun <id>` of the latest **attempt-1** cancelled run per required context (deduped per run id); a run already re-run and still cancelled is skipped — no automatic retry loop.
- Placement: it never touches labels and never dispatches workflows, so it **cannot fight `sweep-stale-validating`** (cancelled conclusions never sweep by design anyway); the documented #637 invariant (merge-validated before sweep) is preserved by prefixing, never interleaving.

**2. This repo's own kicker stub** (`.github/workflows/factory-sm-kicker.yml`): the caller-level global `sm-kicker` group alone would keep superseding pending kickers even after the canonical awf fix is re-pinned — scoped to `sm-kicker-${{ github.sha }}` (effective once the pin bump lands; pin bumps are separate PRs by repo convention).

## Tests

10 new unit tests in the existing `test_smAgent.js` rule-test patterns (rerun+marker shape, rerun-failure posts no marker, CANCELLED-only matching, in-flight skip, once-per-head pacing, attempt-2 no-loop, newest-run-wins, dry-run, no-config skip, and a `sm_github.json` placement pin asserting rule order). Node harness: 178 passed, 1 failed — the single failure is the pre-existing `assert.doesNotThrow` mock gap present on clean `main` (the canonical gate is the pack-release test job). `actionlint` clean. #684/#685/#686 suites untouched and green.

# PR Discussion History

_Previous review discussions for PR #695._

## Review Threads (Inline Comments)

### Thread 1 — `js/smAgent.js`

**ai-teammate** (2026-10-04):
🚨 **BLOCKING: the scan flags a required context as CANCELLED even when a NEWER run already re-stamped it green**

`cancelledRequiredContexts` treats the context as cancelled if **any** check run in the commit's rollup reads `CANCELLED`:

```js
rollup.forEach(function (r) {
    var name = r && (r.name || r.context);
    var concl = r && r.conclusion ? String(r.conclusion).toUpperCase() : null;
    if (name && concl === 'CANCELLED' && contexts.indexOf(name) !== -1) {
        cancelled[name] = true;
    }
});
```

`github_get_commit_check_runs` returns **all** check runs on the commit (verified live: "Get all check runs ... for a commit SHA") — including stale ones from earlier attempts/dispatches. Branch protection resolves each required context by its **latest** check run; this code does not, despite the comment claiming "the check-runs rollup is the source of truth".

Reachable sequence with this repo's own machinery:

1. Validation run A (attempt 1) on head H is cancelled — exactly the #632/#682 class this rule targets (or stale-run cleanup).
2. `revalidate-armed` re-dispatches a fresh run B on H after the 15-min grace → B re-stamps `static`/`gate`/`agents-gate` **green**.
3. Next tick this rule runs **first** (before `merge-validated`), sees A's stale `CANCELLED` check runs, and `gh run rerun`s A + posts the marker — on a head that is already green and mergeable.

Consequences: the merge is delayed a full validation cycle; if the spurious rerun fails (moved base, flake), the freshly re-stamped red hands the PR to `fail_validation` and it gets parked — the rule actively harms the PRs it protects. Same trap after the rule's own remedy: attempt-1 cancelled check runs persist next to attempt-2's, so any tick where the marker read errors (`catch` → `rcReported = false`) re-fires.

Fix (~5 lines): keep only the **latest** check run per required context (max `completed_at`, tie-break by `id`) before testing `=== 'CANCELLED'`, and add a test fixture with a stale-cancelled + fresh-green pair (the current fixtures only ever carry the cancelled runs, which pins the bug).

---

### Thread 2 — `js/smAgent.js`

**ai-teammate** (2026-10-04):
⚠️ **IMPORTANT: once-per-head marker is posted even when the rerun set covers only part of the cancelled contexts**

`rcTargets` can legitimately cover a **subset** of `rcCancelled`: contexts whose cancelled runs are already attempt-2+ (skipped by design), or whose job names don't match any walked run (`jobs?per_page=50` cap, job-name/context drift). The marker is then posted anyway, and from the next tick on the `rcReported` check short-circuits **before** the mapping probe — the head is "remedied" forever while the uncovered contexts still read `CANCELLED` (the exact gh-682 BLOCKED symptom), and even the per-tick `"no rerunnable ... skip"` warn disappears into the marker.

```js
if (rcReported) {
    console.log('  ⏭️  ' + key + ' cancelled checks already re-run for head — waiting on the rerun');
    continue;
}
```

Suggestion: post the marker only when `rcTargets` covers **all** of `rcCancelled` (or list the uncovered contexts in the marker text), so an unmapped context keeps visibly retrying/warning instead of being silently latched shut by a partial remediation. Test to add: two cancelled contexts where only one maps to an attempt-1 run → no marker on that tick.

---

### Thread 3 — `js/unit-tests/test_smAgent.js`

**ai-teammate** (2026-10-04):
⚠️ **IMPORTANT: copy-paste bug in the new test helper — `it[k] = extra` drops the `[k]` index**

```js
function prItem682(n, extra) {
    var it = { key: 'pr-' + n, labels: ['ai_validating'], issueNumber: null,
               prNumber: n, draft: false, branch: 'ai/gh-1202',
               pr: { headSha: '898efd4' } };
    if (extra) { for (var k in extra) { if (extra.hasOwnProperty(k)) it[k] = extra; } }
    return it;
}
```

Every sibling helper in this file does `it[k] = extra[k]` (lines 855, 1682, 1864, 2041) — this copy assigns the whole `extra` object to every key. It is latent today only because every call site is `prItem682(1202)`; the first caller that passes `extra` (e.g. `prItem682(1202, { labels: ['ai_validated'] })`) gets `{ labels: {labels: [...]}, prNumber: {labels: [...]}, ... }` and a silently wrong fixture. One-character fix.

---

### Thread 4 — `js/smAgent.js`

**ai-teammate** (2026-10-04):
💡 **SUGGESTION: `number:` vs `pullRequestId:` — keep one spelling per tool in this file**

This new call site passes `number: ticket.prNumber` to `github_get_pr_comments`, while all 8 other call sites in this file (1573, 1817, 1845, 1993, 2020, 2165, 2979 …) use `pullRequestId:`. Both aliases work against the current dmtools runtime (verified live), but if the tool ever tightens its input schema, every site should already agree — `pullRequestId` is the canonical name per `js/common/trackers.js` ("the number argument keeps the tool's canonical pullRequestId name"). Same payload, just match the file's existing contract.

---

### Thread 5 — `js/smAgent.js`

**ai-teammate** (2026-10-04):
💡 **SUGGESTION: `rcRunIds` is dead code**

```js
var rcRunIds = [];
var rcSeen = {};
rcTargets.forEach(function (t) {
    if (rcSeen[t.runId]) return;
    rcSeen[t.runId] = true;
    rcRunIds.push(t.runId);
```

`rcRunIds` is populated and never read — `rcSeen` alone performs the per-run dedup (and the log line below re-derives the summary from `rcTargets`). Drop the array; less state to misread in an already guard-dense block.

---

### Thread 6 — `js/smAgent.js`

**ai-teammate** (2026-10-04):
💡 **SUGGESTION: both probes cap at `per_page=50` — busy heads can silently exceed the window**

`headWorkflowRuns` (this line) and the per-run jobs probe (line 2774) stop at 50. A long-lived PR head accumulates runs on every push × workflow (the gh-682 evidence alone shows 8+ kicker runs in one 36-second wave), and `actions/runs?head_sha=` returns newest-first — so on a sufficiently busy head the cancelled run can fall outside the first page. Failure mode is quiet: the context still reads `CANCELLED` via the check-runs endpoint, but `rerunTargetsForCancelledContexts` finds no run → `⚠️ ... no rerunnable (attempt-1) cancelled run — skip, retry next tick` forever (no remedy, no marker). Either raise/page the cap for this targeted probe (a filtered `runs?head_sha=` + `conclusion=cancelled` server-side would shrink the payload too), or log the total_count when the window is saturated so the gap is visible.

---

### Thread 7 — `sm_github.json`

**ai-teammate** (2026-10-04):
💡 **SUGGESTION: `limit: 1` drains a cancel-wave one PR per 10-min tick**

The action itself is cheap (a few API reads + an idempotent `gh run rerun` — no workflow dispatch, no budget competition), but the gh-682 evidence shows eight branches' kickers cancelled inside one 36-second wave. At `limit: 1` on the 10-minute SM cadence that wave needs ~80 minutes to drain, with `ai_validated` queue-heads stuck BLOCKED the whole time — the dead-zone cost this PR is trying to eliminate. The sibling bulk rules use `limit: 10` (`sweep-stale-validating`, `silent-update-behind`); consider matching them, the guards (marker, in-flight probe, attempt-1-only) already bound the write side.

---

## Automated Code Review — REQUEST_CHANGES

**Summary**: The gh-682 diagnosis and the kicker concurrency stub are sound, but the new rule's core matching has one blocking bug: `cancelledRequiredContexts` flags a context off **any** historical `CANCELLED` check run instead of the **latest** one (branch-protection semantics), so stale cancelled runs next to a fresh green re-stamp trigger spurious reruns that delay merges and can park a mergeable PR red.

**Key Issues**:
- 🚨 `js/smAgent.js:2733` — stale check-run matching; fix = latest-check-run-per-context before the `CANCELLED` test (+ fixture with stale-cancelled + fresh-green pair)
- ⚠️ `js/smAgent.js:1719` — partial-coverage rerun set still posts the once-per-head marker, permanently la…

# Pull Request Information

- **PR #**: 695
- **URL**: https://github.com/IstiN/dmtools-agents/pull/695
- **Title**: gh-682: standing SM remedy — cancelled required checks re-run themselves (kicker cancel-loop)
- **Author**: IstiN
- **Branch**: `fix/682-rerun-cancelled-checks` → `main`
- **State**: open
- **Files Changed**: 4
- **Additions**: +617
- **Deletions**: -1
- **Created**: 2026-10-04T06:56:26Z
- **Updated**: 2026-10-04T07:54:58Z

## PR Description

Closes #682 (PR 1 of 2 — the kicker-side fix lands in IstiN/dmtools-agentic-workflows; this PR is the standing SM remedy + this repo's own stub scoping).

## Evidence (#682)

- **fa#1202** (head `898efd4`): all 4 kicker push-runs on `ai/gh-1171` CANCELLED 21:43–23:05 as silent-refresh pushes landed; required checks ended CANCELLED → PR BLOCKED until the manual rerun at 23:26.
- **fa#1203**: same pattern twice (23:47, 23:57) — the queue head stalled on it.
- **Still reproducing 2026-10-04 06:21–06:22**: eight branches' kicker runs cancelled inside one 36-second dev-wave (fa run ids 37182568709…37182598010); this repo's own kicker showed the same at 06:36/06:41/06:43.
- Cost on 2026-10-03 alone: 2 dead zones on queue heads + 2 manual reruns.

Mechanism: a queued run in a shared concurrency group **always supersedes the pending one** — *"Any existing pending job or workflow in the same concurrency group, if it exists, will be canceled and the new queued job or workflow will take its place"* (GitHub docs). `cancel-in-progress: false` only shields the RUNNING run. Every silent-refresh push therefore killed the pending kicker, and no rule treated CANCELLED as re-runnable (the #632 class, now triggered by our own refresh machinery).

## What this PR does

**1. Standing rule `rerun-cancelled-checks`** (`sm_github.json`, FIRST in the array):

- match: armed (`ai_validating`) or latched (`ai_validated`) PR; not BEHIND (silent-update refreshes that head), not DIRTY (conflict-rework owns it), not `agent:rework`;
- `localAction rerun_cancelled_checks` (js/smAgent.js):
  - scans the head's check runs — only contexts that currently read **CANCELLED** among `rule.requiredContexts` act (dart: `static`/`gate`/`agents-gate`; fa: the kicker's `kicker / sm-liveness`, `kicker / head-completeness`). Failure paths untouched — red stays `fail_validation` territory;
  - once-per-head marker comment (conflict_rework pacing) citing fa#1202/#1203 + 2026-10-04 06:21, posted AFTER the reruns land (the gh-683 bug C invariant: a failed rerun posts no marker, the next tick retries);
  - **no in-flight run on the head** guard — the `hasActiveDispatchedRun` probe pattern widened to every run on the head (any event): an active run re-stamps the contexts by itself;
  - `gh run rerun <id>` of the latest **attempt-1** cancelled run per required context (deduped per run id); a run already re-run and still cancelled is skipped — no automatic retry loop.
- Placement: it never touches labels and never dispatches workflows, so it **cannot fight `sweep-stale-validating`** (cancelled conclusions never sweep by design anyway); the documented #637 invariant (merge-validated before sweep) is preserved by prefixing, never interleaving.

**2. This repo's own kicker stub** (`.github/workflows/factory-sm-kicker.yml`): the caller-level global `sm-kicker` group alone would keep superseding pending kickers even after the canonical awf fix is re-pinned — scoped to `sm-kicker-${{ github.sha }}` (effective once the pin bump lands; pin bumps are separate PRs by repo convention).

## Tests

10 new unit tests in the existing `test_smAgent.js` rule-test patterns (rerun+marker shape, rerun-failure posts no marker, CANCELLED-only matching, in-flight skip, once-per-head pacing, attempt-2 no-loop, newest-run-wins, dry-run, no-config skip, and a `sm_github.json` placement pin asserting rule order). Node harness: 178 passed, 1 failed — the single failure is the pre-existing `assert.doesNotThrow` mock gap present on clean `main` (the canonical gate is the pack-release test job). `actionlint` clean. #684/#685/#686 suites untouched and green.

# PR Discussion History

_Previous review discussions for PR #695._

## Review Threads (Inline Comments)

### Thread 1 — `js/smAgent.js`

**ai-teammate** (2026-10-04):
🚨 **BLOCKING: the scan flags a required context as CANCELLED even when a NEWER run already re-stamped it green**

`cancelledRequiredContexts` treats the context as cancelled if **any** check run in the commit's rollup reads `CANCELLED`:

```js
rollup.forEach(function (r) {
    var name = r && (r.name || r.context);
    var concl = r && r.conclusion ? String(r.conclusion).toUpperCase() : null;
    if (name && concl === 'CANCELLED' && contexts.indexOf(name) !== -1) {
        cancelled[name] = true;
    }
});
```

`github_get_commit_check_runs` returns **all** check runs on the commit (verified live: "Get all check runs ... for a commit SHA") — including stale ones from earlier attempts/dispatches. Branch protection resolves each required context by its **latest** check run; this code does not, despite the comment claiming "the check-runs rollup is the source of truth".

Reachable sequence with this repo's own machinery:

1. Validation run A (attempt 1) on head H is cancelled — exactly the #632/#682 class this rule targets (or stale-run cleanup).
2. `revalidate-armed` re-dispatches a fresh run B on H after the 15-min grace → B re-stamps `static`/`gate`/`agents-gate` **green**.
3. Next tick this rule runs **first** (before `merge-validated`), sees A's stale `CANCELLED` check runs, and `gh run rerun`s A + posts the marker — on a head that is already green and mergeable.

Consequences: the merge is delayed a full validation cycle; if the spurious rerun fails (moved base, flake), the freshly re-stamped red hands the PR to `fail_validation` and it gets parked — the rule actively harms the PRs it protects. Same trap after the rule's own remedy: attempt-1 cancelled check runs persist next to attempt-2's, so any tick where the marker read errors (`catch` → `rcReported = false`) re-fires.

Fix (~5 lines): keep only the **latest** check run per required context (max `completed_at`, tie-break by `id`) before testing `=== 'CANCELLED'`, and add a test fixture with a stale-cancelled + fresh-green pair (the current fixtures only ever carry the cancelled runs, which pins the bug).

---

### Thread 2 — `js/smAgent.js`

**ai-teammate** (2026-10-04):
⚠️ **IMPORTANT: once-per-head marker is posted even when the rerun set covers only part of the cancelled contexts**

`rcTargets` can legitimately cover a **subset** of `rcCancelled`: contexts whose cancelled runs are already attempt-2+ (skipped by design), or whose job names don't match any walked run (`jobs?per_page=50` cap, job-name/context drift). The marker is then posted anyway, and from the next tick on the `rcReported` check short-circuits **before** the mapping probe — the head is "remedied" forever while the uncovered contexts still read `CANCELLED` (the exact gh-682 BLOCKED symptom), and even the per-tick `"no rerunnable ... skip"` warn disappears into the marker.

```js
if (rcReported) {
    console.log('  ⏭️  ' + key + ' cancelled checks already re-run for head — waiting on the rerun');
    continue;
}
```

Suggestion: post the marker only when `rcTargets` covers **all** of `rcCancelled` (or list the uncovered contexts in the marker text), so an unmapped context keeps visibly retrying/warning instead of being silently latched shut by a partial remediation. Test to add: two cancelled contexts where only one maps to an attempt-1 run → no marker on that tick.

---

### Thread 3 — `js/unit-tests/test_smAgent.js`

**ai-teammate** (2026-10-04):
⚠️ **IMPORTANT: copy-paste bug in the new test helper — `it[k] = extra` drops the `[k]` index**

```js
function prItem682(n, extra) {
    var it = { key: 'pr-' + n, labels: ['ai_validating'], issueNumber: null,
               prNumber: n, draft: false, branch: 'ai/gh-1202',
               pr: { headSha: '898efd4' } };
    if (extra) { for (var k in extra) { if (extra.hasOwnProperty(k)) it[k] = extra; } }
    return it;
}
```

Every sibling helper in this file does `it[k] = extra[k]` (lines 855, 1682, 1864, 2041) — this copy assigns the whole `extra` object to every key. It is latent today only because every call site is `prItem682(1202)`; the first caller that passes `extra` (e.g. `prItem682(1202, { labels: ['ai_validated'] })`) gets `{ labels: {labels: [...]}, prNumber: {labels: [...]}, ... }` and a silently wrong fixture. One-character fix.

---

### Thread 4 — `js/smAgent.js`

**ai-teammate** (2026-10-04):
💡 **SUGGESTION: `number:` vs `pullRequestId:` — keep one spelling per tool in this file**

This new call site passes `number: ticket.prNumber` to `github_get_pr_comments`, while all 8 other call sites in this file (1573, 1817, 1845, 1993, 2020, 2165, 2979 …) use `pullRequestId:`. Both aliases work against the current dmtools runtime (verified live), but if the tool ever tightens its input schema, every site should already agree — `pullRequestId` is the canonical name per `js/common/trackers.js` ("the number argument keeps the tool's canonical pullRequestId name"). Same payload, just match the file's existing contract.

---

### Thread 5 — `js/smAgent.js`

**ai-teammate** (2026-10-04):
💡 **SUGGESTION: `rcRunIds` is dead code**

```js
var rcRunIds = [];
var rcSeen = {};
rcTargets.forEach(function (t) {
    if (rcSeen[t.runId]) return;
    rcSeen[t.runId] = true;
    rcRunIds.push(t.runId);
```

`rcRunIds` is populated and never read — `rcSeen` alone performs the per-run dedup (and the log line below re-derives the summary from `rcTargets`). Drop the array; less state to misread in an already guard-dense block.

---

### Thread 6 — `js/smAgent.js`

**ai-teammate** (2026-10-04):
💡 **SUGGESTION: both probes cap at `per_page=50` — busy heads can silently exceed the window**

`headWorkflowRuns` (this line) and the per-run jobs probe (line 2774) stop at 50. A long-lived PR head accumulates runs on every push × workflow (the gh-682 evidence alone shows 8+ kicker runs in one 36-second wave), and `actions/runs?head_sha=` returns newest-first — so on a sufficiently busy head the cancelled run can fall outside the first page. Either raise/page the cap for this targeted probe (a filtered `runs?head_sha=` + `conclusion=cancelled` server-side would shrink the payload too), or log the total_count when the window is saturated so the gap is visible.

---

### Thread 7 — `sm_github.json`

**ai-teammate** (2026-10-04):
💡 **SUGGESTION: `limit: 1` drains a cancel-wave one PR per 10-min tick**

The action itself is cheap (a few API reads + an idempotent `gh run rerun` — no workflow dispatch, no budget competition), but the gh-682 evidence shows eight branches' kickers cancelled inside one 36-second wave. At `limit: 1` on the 10-minute SM cadence that wave needs ~80 minutes to drain, with `ai_validated` queue-heads stuck BLOCKED the whole time — the dead-zone cost this PR is trying to eliminate. The sibling bulk rules use `limit: 10` (`sweep-stale-validating`, `silent-update-behind`); consider matching them, the guards (marker, in-flight probe, attempt-1-only) already bound the write side.
