## Conventions

### No project-specific content — STRICT RULE

**This is a public, product-agnostic repository. NEVER commit anything company- or customer-specific here.** Violations are a fireable offense and require history rewrite.

Forbidden anywhere in this repo (code, comments, prompts, instructions, tests, docs, commit messages):

- Company, customer, or product names
- Internal hostnames, URLs, IPs, Jira/Confluence links, real ticket keys
- Internal label/branch/repo naming conventions tied to one organization
- File paths pointing to internal repos, internal registry URLs
- Sample data copied from real internal systems

Everything here must be **generic and configurable**: names like `example.com`, `PROJ-123`, `acme`; behavior driven by `customParams` / `.dmtools/config.js` in the consuming repo. Project context goes in the target repo's `.dmtools/config.js` or the corporate orchestrator repo — never here.

**Before every commit**: re-read your diff and check it against this list.

### Agent config structure
- `metadata.contextId` identifies the workflow (used for config composition lookups).
- `preJSAction` / `preCliJSAction` / `postJSAction` — GraalJS hooks that run before/after the CLI agent.
- `cliPrompt` — path to the main prompt markdown.
- `cliPrompts` — additional prompt files appended to the CLI agent input.
- `cliCommands` — shell scripts invoked by dmtools to run the AI CLI.

# Pull Request Information

- **PR #**: 695
- **URL**: https://github.com/IstiN/dmtools-agents/pull/695
- **Title**: gh-682: standing SM remedy — cancelled required checks re-run themselves (kicker cancel-loop)
- **Author**: IstiN
- **Branch**: `fix/682-rerun-cancelled-checks` → `main`
- **State**: open
- **Files Changed**: 4
- **Additions**: +617
- **Deletions**: -1
- **Created**: 2026-10-04T06:56:26Z
- **Updated**: 2026-10-04T07:54:58Z

## PR Description

Closes #682 (PR 1 of 2 — the kicker-side fix lands in IstiN/dmtools-agentic-workflows; this PR is the standing SM remedy + this repo's own stub scoping).

## Evidence (#682)

- **fa#1202** (head `898efd4`): all 4 kicker push-runs on `ai/gh-1171` CANCELLED 21:43–23:05 as silent-refresh pushes landed; required checks ended CANCELLED → PR BLOCKED until the manual rerun at 23:26.
- **fa#1203**: same pattern twice (23:47, 23:57) — the queue head stalled on it.
- **Still reproducing 2026-10-04 06:21–06:22**: eight branches' kicker runs cancelled inside one 36-second dev-wave (fa run ids 37182568709…37182598010); this repo's own kicker showed the same at 06:36/06:41/06:43.
- Cost on 2026-10-03 alone: 2 dead zones on queue heads + 2 manual reruns.

Mechanism: a queued run in a shared concurrency group **always supersedes the pending one** — *"Any existing pending job or workflow in the same concurrency group, if it exists, will be canceled and the new queued job or workflow will take its place"* (GitHub docs). `cancel-in-progress: false` only shields the RUNNING run. Every silent-refresh push therefore killed the pending kicker, and no rule treated CANCELLED as re-runnable (the #632 class, now triggered by our own refresh machinery).

## What this PR does

**1. Standing rule `rerun-cancelled-checks`** (`sm_github.json`, FIRST in the array):

- match: armed (`ai_validating`) or latched (`ai_validated`) PR; not BEHIND (silent-update refreshes that head), not DIRTY (conflict-rework owns it), not `agent:rework`;
- `localAction rerun_cancelled_checks` (js/smAgent.js):
  - scans the head's check runs — only contexts that currently read **CANCELLED** among `rule.requiredContexts` act (dart: `static`/`gate`/`agents-gate`; fa: the kicker's `kicker / sm-liveness`, `kicker / head-completeness`). Failure paths untouched — red stays `fail_validation` territory;
  - once-per-head marker comment (conflict_rework pacing) citing fa#1202/#1203 + 2026-10-04 06:21, posted AFTER the reruns land (the gh-683 bug C invariant: a failed rerun posts no marker, the next tick retries);
  - **no in-flight run on the head** guard — the `hasActiveDispatchedRun` probe pattern widened to every run on the head (any event): an active run re-stamps the contexts by itself;
  - `gh run rerun <id>` of the latest **attempt-1** cancelled run per required context (deduped per run id); a run already re-run and still cancelled is skipped — no automatic retry loop.
- Placement: it never touches labels and never dispatches workflows, so it **cannot fight `sweep-stale-validating`** (cancelled conclusions never sweep by design anyway); the documented #637 invariant (merge-validated before sweep) is preserved by prefixing, never interleaving.

**2. This repo's own kicker stub** (`.github/workflows/factory-sm-kicker.yml`): the caller-level global `sm-kicker` group alone would keep superseding pending kickers even after the canonical awf fix is re-pinned — scoped to `sm-kicker-${{ github.sha }}` (effective once the pin bump lands; pin bumps are separate PRs by repo convention).

## Tests

10 new unit tests in the existing `test_smAgent.js` rule-test patterns (rerun+marker shape, rerun-failure posts no marker, CANCELLED-only matching, in-flight skip, once-per-head pacing, attempt-2 no-loop, newest-run-wins, dry-run, no-config skip, and a `sm_github.json` placement pin asserting rule order). Node harness: 178 passed, 1 failed — the single failure is the pre-existing `assert.doesNotThrow` mock gap present on clean `main` (the canonical gate is the pack-release test job). `actionlint` clean. #684/#685/#686 suites untouched and green.

# PR Discussion History

_Previous review discussions for PR #695._

## Review Threads (Inline Comments)

### Thread 1 — `js/smAgent.js`

**ai-teammate** (2026-10-04):
🚨 **BLOCKING: the scan flags a required context as CANCELLED even when a NEWER run already re-stamped it green**

`cancelledRequiredContexts` treats the context as cancelled if **any** check run in the commit's rollup reads `CANCELLED`:

```js
rollup.forEach(function (r) {
    var name = r && (r.name || r.context);
    var concl = r && r.conclusion ? String(r.conclusion).toUpperCase() : null;
    if (name && concl === 'CANCELLED' && contexts.indexOf(name) !== -1) {
        cancelled[name] = true;
    }
});
```

`github_get_commit_check_runs` returns **all** check runs on the commit (verified live: "Get all check runs ... for a commit SHA") — including stale ones from earlier attempts/dispatches. Branch protection resolves each required context by its **latest** check run; this code does not, despite the comment claiming "the check-runs rollup is the source of truth".

Reachable sequence with this repo's own machinery:

1. Validation run A (attempt 1) on head H is cancelled — exactly the #632/#682 class this rule targets (or stale-run cleanup).
2. `revalidate-armed` re-dispatches a fresh run B on H after the 15-min grace → B re-stamps `static`/`gate`/`agents-gate` **green**.
3. Next tick this rule runs **first** (before `merge-validated`), sees A's stale `CANCELLED` check runs, and `gh run rerun`s A + posts the marker — on a head that is already green and mergeable.

# Pull Request Information

- **PR #**: 695
- **URL**: https://github.com/IstiN/dmtools-agents/pull/695
- **Title**: gh-682: standing SM remedy — cancelled required checks re-run themselves (kicker cancel-loop)
- **Author**: IstiN
- **Branch**: `fix/682-rerun-cancelled-checks` → `main`
- **State**: open
- **Files Changed**: 4
- **Additions**: +617
- **Deletions**: -1
- **Created**: 2026-10-04T06:56:26Z
- **Updated**: 2026-10-04T07:54:58Z

## PR Description

Closes #682 (PR 1 of 2 — the kicker-side fix lands in IstiN/dmtools-agentic-workflows; this PR is the standing SM remedy + this repo's own stub scoping).

## Evidence (#682)

- **fa#1202** (head `898efd4`): all 4 kicker push-runs on `ai/gh-1171` CANCELLED 21:43–23:05 as silent-refresh pushes landed; required checks ended CANCELLED → PR BLOCKED until the manual rerun at 23:26.
- **fa#1203**: same pattern twice (23:47, 23:57) — the queue head stalled on it.
- **Still reproducing 2026-10-04 06:21–06:22**: eight branches' kicker runs cancelled inside one 36-second dev-wave (fa run ids 37182568709…37182598010); this repo's own kicker showed the same at 06:36/06:41/06:43.
- Cost on 2026-10-03 alone: 2 dead zones on queue heads + 2 manual reruns.

Mechanism: a queued run in a shared concurrency group **always supersedes the pending one** — *"Any existing pending job or workflow in the same concurrency group, if it exists, will be canceled and the new queued job or workflow will take its place"* (GitHub docs). `cancel-in-progress: false` only shields the RUNNING run. Every silent-refresh push therefore killed the pending kicker, and no rule treated CANCELLED as re-runnable (the #632 class, now triggered by our own refresh machinery).

## What this PR does

**1. Standing rule `rerun-cancelled-checks`** (`sm_github.json`, FIRST in the array):

- match: armed (`ai_validating`) or latched (`ai_validated`) PR; not BEHIND (silent-update refreshes that head), not DIRTY (conflict-rework owns it), not `agent:rework`;
- `localAction rerun_cancelled_checks` (js/smAgent.js):
  - scans the head's check runs — only contexts that currently read **CANCELLED** among `rule.requiredContexts` act (dart: `static`/`gate`/`agents-gate`; fa: the kicker's `kicker / sm-liveness`, `kicker / head-completeness`). Failure paths untouched — red stays `fail_validation` territory;
  - once-per-head marker comment (conflict_rework pacing) citing fa#1202/#1203 + 2026-10-04 06:21, posted AFTER the reruns land (the gh-683 bug C invariant: a failed rerun posts no marker, the next tick retries);
  - **no in-flight run on the head** guard — the `hasActiveDispatchedRun` probe pattern widened to every run on the head (any event): an active run re-stamps the contexts by itself;
  - `gh run rerun <id>` of the latest **attempt-1** cancelled run per required context (deduped per run id); a run already re-run and still cancelled is skipped — no automatic retry loop.
- Placement: it never touches labels and never dispatches workflows, so it **cannot fight `sweep-stale-validating`** (cancelled conclusions never sweep by design anyway); the documented #637 invariant (merge-validated before sweep) is preserved by prefixing, never interleaving.

**2. This repo's own kicker stub** (`.github/workflows/factory-sm-kicker.yml`): the caller-level global `sm-kicker` group alone would keep superseding pending kickers even after the canonical awf fix is re-pinned — scoped to `sm-kicker-${{ github.sha }}` (effective once the pin bump lands; pin bumps are separate PRs by repo convention).

## Tests

10 new unit tests in the existing `test_smAgent.js` rule-test patterns (rerun+marker shape, rerun-failure posts no marker, CANCELLED-only matching, in-flight skip, once-per-head pacing, attempt-2 no-loop, newest-run-wins, dry-run, no-config skip, and a `sm_github.json` placement pin asserting rule order). Node harness: 178 passed, 1 failed — the single failure is the pre-existing `assert.doesNotThrow` mock gap present on clean `main` (the canonical gate is the pack-release test job). `actionlint` clean. #684/#685/#686 suites untouched and green.

name: SM kicker

run-name: '🥁 kicker ${{ github.event_name }} ${{ github.ref_name }}'

on:
  push:
    branches-ignore: [main]
  schedule:
    - cron: '13,43 * * * *'

permissions:
  actions: write
  contents: read
  pull-requests: read

  # global group below already ran with cancel-in-progress:false, yet
  # kicker runs kept dying cancelled in chains. cancel-in-progress only
  # shields the RUNNING run — a queued run in the same group ALWAYS
  # supersedes (cancels) the pending one (GitHub docs: "Any existing
  # pending job or workflow in the same concurrency group, if it exists,
  # will be canceled and the new queued job or workflow will take its
  # place"). One global group meant every push anywhere (silent refresh,
  # factory-data snapshots, dev waves) cancelled every other branch's

# Pull Request Information

- **PR #**: 695
- **URL**: https://github.com/IstiN/dmtools-agents/pull/695
- **Title**: gh-682: standing SM remedy — cancelled required checks re-run themselves (kicker cancel-loop)
- **Author**: IstiN
- **Branch**: `fix/682-rerun-cancelled-checks` → `main`
- **State**: open
- **Files Changed**: 4
- **Additions**: +617
- **Deletions**: -1
- **Created**: 2026-10-04T06:56:26Z
- **Updated**: 2026-10-04T07:54:58Z

## PR Description

Closes #682 (PR 1 of 2 — the kicker-side fix lands in IstiN/dmtools-agentic-workflows; this PR is the standing SM remedy + this repo's own stub scoping).

## Evidence (#682)

- **fa#1202** (head `898efd4`): all 4 kicker push-runs on `ai/gh-1171` CANCELLED 21:43–23:05 as silent-refresh pushes landed; required checks ended CANCELLED → PR BLOCKED until the manual rerun at 23:26.
- **fa#1203**: same pattern twice (23:47, 23:57) — the queue head stalled on it.
- **Still reproducing 2026-10-04 06:21–06:22**: eight branches' kicker runs cancelled inside one 36-second dev-wave (fa run ids 37182568709…37182598010); this repo's own kicker showed the same at 06:36/06:41/06:43.
- Cost on 2026-10-03 alone: 2 dead zones on queue heads + 2 manual reruns.

Mechanism: a queued run in a shared concurrency group **always supersedes the pending one** — *"Any existing pending job or workflow in the same concurrency group, if it exists, will be canceled and the new queued job or workflow will take its place"* (GitHub docs). `cancel-in-progress: false` only shields the RUNNING run. Every silent-refresh push therefore killed the pending kicker, and no rule treated CANCELLED as re-runnable (the #632 class, now triggered by our own refresh machinery).

## What this PR does

**1. Standing rule `rerun-cancelled-checks`** (`sm_github.json`, FIRST in the array):

- match: armed (`ai_validating`) or latched (`ai_validated`) PR; not BEHIND (silent-update refreshes that head), not DIRTY (conflict-rework owns it), not `agent:rework`;
- `localAction rerun_cancelled_checks` (js/smAgent.js):
  - scans the head's check runs — only contexts that currently read **CANCELLED** among `rule.requiredContexts` act (dart: `static`/`gate`/`agents-gate`; fa: the kicker's `kicker / sm-liveness`, `kicker / head-completeness`). Failure paths untouched — red stays `fail_validation` territory;
  - once-per-head marker comment (conflict_rework pacing) citing fa#1202/#1203 + 2026-10-04 06:21, posted AFTER the reruns land (the gh-683 bug C invariant: a failed rerun posts no marker, the next tick retries);
  - **no in-flight run on the head** guard — the `hasActiveDispatchedRun` probe pattern widened to every run on the head (any event): an active run re-stamps the contexts by itself;
  - `gh run rerun <id>` of the latest **attempt-1** cancelled run per required context (deduped per run id); a run already re-run and still cancelled is skipped — no automatic retry loop.
- Placement: it never touches labels and never dispatches workflows, so it **cannot fight `sweep-stale-validating`** (cancelled conclusions never sweep by design anyway); the documented #637 invariant (merge-validated before sweep) is preserved by prefixing, never interleaving.

**2. This repo's own kicker stub** (`.github/workflows/factory-sm-kicker.yml`): the caller-level global `sm-kicker` group alone would keep superseding pending kickers even after the canonical awf fix is re-pinned — scoped to `sm-kicker-${{ github.sha }}` (effective once the pin bump lands; pin bumps are separate PRs by repo convention).

## Tests

10 new unit tests in the existing `test_smAgent.js` rule-test patterns (rerun+marker shape, rerun-failure posts no marker, CANCELLED-only matching, in-flight skip, once-per-head pacing, attempt-2 no-loop, newest-run-wins, dry-run, no-config skip, and a `sm_github.json` placement pin asserting rule order). Node harness: 178 passed, 1 failed — the single failure is the pre-existing `assert.doesNotThrow` mock gap present on clean `main` (the canonical gate is the pack-release test job). `actionlint` clean. #684/#685/#686 suites untouched and green.

# PR Discussion History

_Previous review discussions for PR #695._

## Review Threads (Inline Comments)

### Thread 1 — `js/smAgent.js`

**ai-teammate** (2026-10-04):
🚨 **BLOCKING: the scan flags a required context as CANCELLED even when a NEWER run already re-stamped it green**

`cancelledRequiredContexts` treats the context as cancelled if **any** check run in the commit's rollup reads `CANCELLED`:

```js
rollup.forEach(function (r) {
    var name = r && (r.name || r.context);
    var concl = r && r.conclusion ? String(r.conclusion).toUpperCase() : null;
    if (name && concl === 'CANCELLED' && contexts.indexOf(name) !== -1) {
        cancelled[name] = true;
    }
});
```

`github_get_commit_check_runs` returns **all** check runs on the commit (verified live: "Get all check runs ... for a commit SHA") — including stale ones from earlier attempts/dispatches. Branch protection resolves each required context by its **latest** check run; this code does not, despite the comment claiming "the check-runs rollup is the source of truth".

Reachable sequence with this repo's own machinery:

1. Validation run A (attempt 1) on head H is cancelled — exactly the #632/#682 class this rule targets (or stale-run cleanup).
2. `revalidate-armed` re-dispatches a fresh run B on H after the 15-min grace → B re-stamps `static`/`gate`/`agents-gate` **green**.
3. Next tick this rule runs **first** (before `merge-validated`), sees A's stale `CANCELLED` check runs, and `gh run rerun`s A + posts the marker — on a head that is already green and mergeable.

Consequences: the merge is delayed a full validation cycle; if the spurious rerun fails (moved base, flake), the freshly re-stamped red hands the PR to `fail_validation` and it gets parked — the rule actively harms the PRs it protects. Same trap after the rule's own remedy: attempt-1 cancelled check runs persist next to attempt-2's, so any tick where the marker read errors (`catch` → `rcReported = false`) re-fires.

Fix (~5 lines): keep only the **latest** check run per required context (max `completed_at`, tie-break by `id`) before testing `=== 'CANCELLED'`, and add a test fixture with a stale-cancelled + fresh-green pair (the current fixtures only ever carry the cancelled runs, which pins the bug).

---

### Thread 2 — `js/smAgent.js`

**ai-teammate** (2026-10-04):
⚠️ **IMPORTANT: once-per-head marker is posted even when the rerun set covers only part of the cancelled contexts**

`rcTargets` can legitimately cover a **subset** of `rcCancelled`: contexts whose cancelled runs are already attempt-2+ (skipped by design), or whose job names don't match any walked run (`jobs?per_page=50` cap, job-name/context drift). The marker is then posted anyway, and from the next tick on the `rcReported` check short-circuits **before** the mapping probe — the head is "remedied" forever while the uncovered contexts still read `CANCELLED` (the exact gh-682 BLOCKED symptom), and even the per-tick `"no rerunnable ... skip"` warn disappears into the marker.

```js
if (rcReported) {
    console.log('  ⏭️  ' + key + ' cancelled checks already re-run for head — waiting on the rerun');
    continue;
}
```

Suggestion: post the marker only when `rcTargets` covers **all** of `rcCancelled` (or list the uncovered contexts in the marker text), so an unmapped context keeps visibly retrying/warning instead of being silently latched shut by a partial remediation. Test to add: two cancelled contexts where only one maps to an attempt-1 run → no marker on that tick.

---

### Thread 3 — `js/unit-tests/test_smAgent.js`

**ai-teammate** (2026-10-04):
⚠️ **IMPORTANT: copy-paste bug in the new test helper — `it[k] = extra` drops the `[k]` index**

```js
function prItem682(n, extra) {
    var it = { key: 'pr-' + n, labels: ['ai_validating'], issueNumber: null,
               prNumber: n, draft: false, branch: 'ai/gh-1202',
               pr: { headSha: '898efd4' } };
    if (extra) { for (var k in extra) { if (extra.hasOwnProperty(k)) it[k] = extra; } }
    return it;
}
```

Every sibling helper in this file does `it[k] = extra[k]` (lines 855, 1682, 1864, 2041) — this copy assigns the whole `extra` object to every key. It is latent today only because every call site is `prItem682(1202)`; the first caller that passes `extra` (e.g. `prItem682(1202, { labels: ['ai_validated'] })`) gets `{ labels: {labels: [...]}, prNumber: {labels: [...]}, ... }` and a silently wrong fixture. One-character fix.

---

### Thread 4 — `js/smAgent.js`

**ai-teammate** (2026-10-04):
💡 **SUGGESTION: `number:` vs `pullRequestId:` — keep one spelling per tool in this file**

This new call site passes `number: ticket.prNumber` to `github_get_pr_comments`, while all 8 other call sites in this file (1573, 1817, 1845, 1993, 2020, 2165, 2979 …) use `pullRequestId:`. Both aliases work against the current dmtools runtime (verified live), but if the tool ever tightens its input schema, every site should already agree — `pullRequestId` is the canonical name per `js/common/trackers.js` ("the number argument keeps the tool's canonical pullRequestId name"). Same payload, just match the file's existing contract.

---

### Thread 5 — `js/smAgent.js`

**ai-teammate** (2026-10-04):
💡 **SUGGESTION: `rcRunIds` is dead code**

```js
var rcRunIds = [];
var rcSeen = {};
rcTargets.forEach(function (t) {
    if (rcSeen[t.runId]) return;
    rcSeen[t.runId] = true;
    rcRunIds.push(t.runId);
```

`rcRunIds` is populated and never read — `rcSeen` alone performs the per-run dedup (and the log line below re-derives the summary from `rcTargets`). Drop the array; less state to misread in an already guard-dense block.

---

### Thread 6 — `js/smAgent.js`

**ai-teammate** (2026-10-04):
💡 **SUGGESTION: both probes cap at `per_page=50` — busy heads can silently exceed the window**

`headWorkflowRuns` (this line) and the per-run jobs probe (line 2774) stop at 50. A long-lived PR head accumulates runs on every push × workflow (the gh-682 evidence alone shows 8+ kicker runs in one 36-second wave), and `actions/runs?head_sha=` returns newest-first — so on a sufficiently busy head the cancelled run can fall outside the first page. Either raise/page the cap for this targeted probe (a filtered `runs?head_sha=` + `conclusion=cancelled` server-side would shrink the payload too), or log the total_count when the window is saturated so the gap is visible.

---

### Thread 7 — `sm_github.json`

**ai-teammate** (2026-10-04):
💡 **SUGGESTION: `limit: 1` drains a cancel-wave one PR per 10-min tick**

The action itself is cheap (a few API reads + an idempotent `gh run rerun` — no workflow dispatch, no budget competition), but the gh-682 evidence shows eight branches' kickers cancelled inside one 36-second wave. At `limit: 1` on the 10-minute SM cadence that wave needs ~80 minutes to drain, with `ai_validated` queue-heads stuck BLOCKED the whole time — the dead-zone cost this PR is trying to eliminate. The sibling bulk rules use `limit: 10` (`sweep-stale-validating`, `silent-update-behind`); consider matching them, the guards (marker, in-flight probe, attempt-1-only) already bound the write side.

# SM kicker — thin stub over the canonical watchdog in the factory home.
# All logic (sm-liveness + head-completeness) lives in
# IstiN/dmtools-agentic-workflows/.github/workflows/factory-sm-kicker.yml.

# required context is the `crap` job.
name: SM kicker

run-name: '🥁 kicker ${{ github.event_name }} ${{ github.ref_name }}'

on:
  push:
    branches-ignore: [main]
  schedule:
    - cron: '13,43 * * * *'
  workflow_dispatch:

permissions:
  actions: write
  contents: read
  pull-requests: read
  checks: read

concurrency:
  # dmtools-agents#682 (live fa#1202/#1203 2026-10-03, still reproducing
  # 2026-10-04 06:21–06:22 in THIS repo — runs 06:36/06:41/06:43): the
  # global group below already ran with cancel-in-progress:false, yet
  # kicker runs kept dying cancelled in chains. cancel-in-progress only
  # shields the RUNNING run — a queued run in the same group ALWAYS
  # supersedes (cancels) the pending one (GitHub docs: "Any existing
  # pending job or workflow in the same concurrency group, if it exists,
  # will be canceled and the new queued job or workflow will take its
  # place"). One global group meant every push anywhere (silent refresh,
  # factory-data snapshots, dev waves) cancelled every other branch's
  # pending kicker. Per-head-SHA group: no push can displace another
  # push's kicker — a queued kicker that is about to dispatch a tick
  # always gets to run (canonical fix + consumer notes: IstiN/
  # dmtools-agentic-workflows factory-sm-kicker.yml). Effective once the
  # canonical pin is bumped (separate PR): until then the called
  # workflow's own global group still supersedes.
  group: sm-kicker-${{ github.sha }}
  cancel-in-progress: false

jobs:
  kicker:
    uses: IstiN/dmtools-agentic-workflows/.github/workflows/factory-sm-kicker.yml@6e8e40eae1cd0f64bedef166b7b6eb92c76c8485
    with:
      sm_workflow: machine-sm.yml
      ci_workflow: quality.yml
      ci_display_name: Quality
      required_contexts: crap

- The kicker workflow has `schedule` (every 30 min: 13,43 *) and `push` (branches-ignore main) and `workflow_dispatch`. Per-SHA group: scheduled runs on the default branch (main) — github.sha for schedule = latest commit on main. If main is quiet, consecutive scheduled kickers share the same SHA → same group → they queue (cancel-in-progress:false) and ALL run serially. Previously: newest superseded pending → only newest ran. So on a quiet main, each scheduled tick now executes every 30 min anyway (13 and 43 = every 30 min, runs take <1 min) — queueing would only matter if a run takes >30 min, which it doesn't. Actually wait — 13,43 means twice an hour. Runs are minutes apart (30 min). No queueing risk. And on dev waves with pushes, each SHA gets its own kicker → the fix. The `workflow_dispatch` on the same SHA twice → queue, fine.

So the workflow change is sound. The schedule edge is negligible — not worth reporting? Per "exhaustive single pass" I could note it, but it must be actionable. Honestly it's a non-issue: 30-min cadence, sub-minute runs. Skip.

## Conventions

### No project-specific content — STRICT RULE

**This is a public, product-agnostic repository. NEVER commit anything company- or customer-specific here.** Violations are a fireable offense and require history rewrite.

Forbidden anywhere in this repo (code, comments, prompts, instructions, tests, docs, commit messages):

- Company, customer, or product names
- Internal hostnames, URLs, IPs, Jira/Confluence links, real ticket keys
- Internal label/branch/repo naming conventions tied to one organization
- File paths pointing to internal repos, internal registry URLs
- Sample data copied from real internal systems

Everything here must be **generic and configurable**: names like `example.com`, `PROJ-123`, `acme`; behavior driven by `customParams` / `.dmtools/config.js` in the consuming repo. Project context goes in the target repo's `.dmtools/config.js` or the corporate orchestrator repo — never here.

**Before every commit**: re-read your diff and check it against this list.

### Agent config structure
- `metadata.contextId` identifies the workflow (used for config composition lookups).
- `preJSAction` / `preCliJSAction` / `postJSAction` — GraalJS hooks that run before/after the CLI agent.
- `cliPrompt` — path to the main prompt markdown.
- `cliPrompts` — additional prompt files appended to the CLI agent input.
- `cliCommands` — shell scripts invoked by dmtools to run the AI CLI.

### Label-based idempotency

re-read changed files,
surface ALL remaining issues"] EXHAUST --> OUTPUT["8. Write outputs:
pr_review.json · pr_review_general.md · pr_review_comments/*.md"] OUTPUT --> END([End]) ``` ## 1. Input context — MANDATORY reading order ```mermaid flowchart TD subgraph PR_CONTEXT["⚠️ PR-specific files (read first)"] P1["1️⃣ instruction.md (repo root) — project stack, conventions"] P2["2️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_info.md — PR title, author, branch, description"] P3["3️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_diff.txt — the diff to review"] P4["4️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_files.txt — list of changed files"] P5["5️⃣ input/TICKET/ci_failures.md — CI failures = BLOCKING (last 500 lines)"] P5_FULL["5️⃣ input/TICKET/ci_failures_full.log — full CI logs"] P6["6️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_discussions.md + pr_discussions_raw.json — existing comments"] P1 --> P2 --> P3 --> P4 --> P5 --> P5_FULL --> P6 end subgraph TICKET_CONTEXT["Ticket context (for understanding PR purpose)"] T1["7️⃣ input/TICKET/ticket.md — linked ticket description, ACs"] T2["8️⃣ input/TICKET/comments.md — ticket discussion if present"] T3["9️⃣ input/TICKET/parent-*.md — parent story context"] T4["🔟 input/TICKET/confluence/*.md — linked specifications"] T1 --> T2 --> T3 --> T4 end subgraph RULE["⚠️ Rule"] R1["If file exists in input/ → read locally, do NOT re-fetch via dmtools"] end PR_CONTEXT --> TICKET_CONTEXT --> RULE ``` Read PR files to understand WHAT changed. Read ticket files to understand WHY it changed and verify against requirements. ## 2. Diff checklist — apply to `pr_diff.txt` For every hunk, ask at least these questions: - [ ] Does the change match the ticket scope? Any scope creep? - [ ] Are new or changed public APIs contract-safe for existing callers? - [ ] Is user/external input validated, sanitized, or escaped? - [ ] Are secrets, tokens, or PATs handled safely — not logged, not interpolated into shell scripts? - [ ] Are new or modified files present under `testing/` in a non-test-automation PR? - [ ] Is dead code, unused imports, or obvious duplication introduced? - [ ] Are error paths handled, or are failures silently swallowed? - [ ] Are new dependencies justified and compatible with the existing stack? - [ ] Beyond blockers: what other maintainability, correctness, or quality improvements are visible in the changed code? ## 3. Changed-file deep read Do not review from the diff alone. Read the full content of every changed file: - imports and dependencies - class/method responsibilities and adherence to SRP / OOP principles - naming consistency with the rest of the codebase - error handling, logging, and edge cases - test coverage for changed behavior - backward-compatibility and migration impact ## 4. Impact analysis (CodeGraph or grep fallback) Use CodeGraph to find "what could break": - `codegraph_callers` / `codegraph_callees` on modified public symbols - `codegraph_search` for: `PAT_TOKEN`, `secrets.`, `github.token`, `previousViewModel` - `codegraph_impact` before flagging architectural changes **If CodeGraph unavailable**, use grep and document it: ```bash grep -rn "changedFunctionName" --include="*.ts" . grep -rn "secrets\.\|github\.token" . ``` ## 5. Review dimensions Rate the PR across all relevant dimensions: | Dimension | What to check | |---|---| | **Security** | injection, unsafe interpolation, secret leakage, missing permissions, unsafe defaults | | **Architecture / OOP** | SRP, coupling, abstraction consistency, provider/repository boundaries | | **Code quality** | naming, complexity, error handling, logging, comments | | **Tests** | coverage for new/changed paths, meaningful assertions, no brittle string-only tests | | **Duplication** | copy-paste, duplicated logic across files, duplicated configuration | | **Backward compatibility** | public API changes, migration paths, default behavior | | **Performance** | unnecessary rebuilds, heavy sync operations, missing timeouts | | **Workflow / CI safety** | (when `.github/workflows/` changes) secret declarations, ref pinning, permissions, timeouts | ## 6. Severity classification Classify every finding before writing outputs: - **BLOCKING** — merge would cause a bug, security issue, data loss, or CI break. Must be fixed. - **IMPORTANT** — real maintainability or correctness issue. Strongly prefer fixing before merge. - **SUGGESTION** — optional improvement, style, or future polish. Does not block merge. When in doubt, start one level higher; downgrade only after confirming the risk is negligible. ## 7. Exhaustive single-pass review Treat **every** review as the final and only review pass. The author will not get another chance to catch missed findings cheaply. - Do not defer SUGGESTION or IMPORTANT items to a later round because a BLOCKING issue exists. - After classifying all findings, re-read every changed file and ask: *"What else is improvable here?"* - Before writing outputs, verify that no obvious quality, maintainability, or correctness issue was left unreported. - Aim to surface the maximum number of actionable findings in this single iteration. ## 8. Findings on unchanged code outside the diff belong in `outputs/pr_review_general.md`, not as inline comments. # Pull Request Information

- **PR #**: 695
- **URL**: https://github.com/IstiN/dmtools-agents/pull/695
- **Title**: gh-682: standing SM remedy — cancelled required checks re-run themselves (kicker cancel-loop)
- **Author**: IstiN
- **Branch**: `fix/682-rerun-cancelled-checks` → `main`
- **State**: open
- **Files Changed**: 4
- **Additions**: +617
- **Deletions**: -1
- **Created**: 2026-10-04T06:56:26Z
- **Updated**: 2026-10-04T07:54:58Z

## PR Description

Closes #682 (PR 1 of 2 — the kicker-side fix lands in IstiN/dmtools-agentic-workflows; this PR is the standing SM remedy + this repo's own stub scoping).

## Evidence (#682)

- **fa#1202** (head `898efd4`): all 4 kicker push-runs on `ai/gh-1171` CANCELLED 21:43–23:05 as silent-refresh pushes landed; required checks ended CANCELLED → PR BLOCKED until the manual rerun at 23:26.
- **fa#1203**: same pattern twice (23:47, 23:57) — the queue head stalled on it.
- **Still reproducing 2026-10-04 06:21–06:22**: eight branches' kicker runs cancelled inside one 36-second dev-wave (fa run ids 37182568709…37182598010); this repo's own kicker showed the same at 06:36/06:41/06:43.
- Cost on 2026-10-03 alone: 2 dead zones on queue heads + 2 manual reruns.

Mechanism: a queued run in a shared concurrency group **always supersedes the pending one** — *"Any existing pending job or workflow in the same concurrency group, if it exists, will be canceled and the new queued job or workflow will take its place"* (GitHub docs). `cancel-in-progress: false` only shields the RUNNING run. Every silent-refresh push therefore killed the pending kicker, and no rule treated CANCELLED as re-runnable (the #632 class, now triggered by our own refresh machinery).

## What this PR does

**1. Standing rule `rerun-cancelled-checks`** (`sm_github.json`, FIRST in the array):

- match: armed (`ai_validating`) or latched (`ai_validated`) PR; not BEHIND (silent-update refreshes that head), not DIRTY (conflict-rework owns it), not `agent:rework`;
- `localAction rerun_cancelled_checks` (js/smAgent.js):
  - scans the head's check runs — only contexts that currently read **CANCELLED** among `rule.requiredContexts` act (dart: `static`/`gate`/`agents-gate`; fa: the kicker's `kicker / sm-liveness`, `kicker / head-completeness`). Failure paths untouched — red stays `fail_validation` territory;
  - once-per-head marker comment (conflict_rework pacing) citing fa#1202/#1203 + 2026-10-04 06:21, posted AFTER the reruns land (the gh-683 bug C invariant: a failed rerun posts no marker, the next tick retries);
  - **no in-flight run on the head** guard — the `hasActiveDispatchedRun` probe pattern widened to every run on the head (any event): an active run re-stamps the contexts by itself;
  - `gh run rerun <id>` of the latest **attempt-1** cancelled run per required context (deduped per run id); a run already re-run and still cancelled is skipped — no automatic retry loop.
- Placement: it never touches labels and never dispatches workflows, so it **cannot fight `sweep-stale-validating`** (cancelled conclusions never sweep by design anyway); the documented #637 invariant (merge-validated before sweep) is preserved by prefixing, never interleaving.

**2. This repo's own kicker stub** (`.github/workflows/factory-sm-kicker.yml`): the caller-level global `sm-kicker` group alone would keep superseding pending kickers even after the canonical awf fix is re-pinned — scoped to `sm-kicker-${{ github.sha }}` (effective once the pin bump lands; pin bumps are separate PRs by repo convention).

## Tests

10 new unit tests in the existing `test_smAgent.js` rule-test patterns (rerun+marker shape, rerun-failure posts no marker, CANCELLED-only matching, in-flight skip, once-per-head pacing, attempt-2 no-loop, newest-run-wins, dry-run, no-config skip, and a `sm_github.json` placement pin asserting rule order). Node harness: 178 passed, 1 failed — the single failure is the pre-existing `assert.doesNotThrow` mock gap present on clean `main` (the canonical gate is the pack-release test job). `actionlint` clean. #684/#685/#686 suites untouched and green.

# PR Discussion History

_Previous review discussions for PR #695._

## Review Threads (Inline Comments)

### Thread 1 — `js/smAgent.js`

**ai-teammate** (2026-10-04):
🚨 **BLOCKING: the scan flags a required context as CANCELLED even when a NEWER run already re-stamped it green**

`cancelledRequiredContexts` treats the context as cancelled if **any** check run in the commit's rollup reads `CANCELLED`:

```js
rollup.forEach(function (r) {
    var name = r && (r.name || r.context);
    var concl = r && r.conclusion ? String(r.conclusion).toUpperCase() : null;
    if (name && concl === 'CANCELLED' && contexts.indexOf(name) !== -1) {
        cancelled[name] = true;
    }
});
```

`github_get_commit_check_runs` returns **all** check runs on the commit (verified live: "Get all check runs ... for a commit SHA") — including stale ones from earlier attempts/dispatches. Branch protection resolves each required context by its **latest** check run; this code does not, despite the comment claiming "the check-runs rollup is the source of truth".

Reachable sequence with this repo's own machinery:

1. Validation run A (attempt 1) on head H is cancelled — exactly the #632/#682 class this rule targets (or stale-run cleanup).
2. `revalidate-armed` re-dispatches a fresh run B on H after the 15-min grace → B re-stamps `static`/`gate`/`agents-gate` **green**.
3. Next tick this rule runs **first** (before `merge-validated`), sees A's stale `CANCELLED` check runs, and `gh run rerun`s A + posts the marker — on a head that is already green and mergeable.

Consequences: the merge is delayed a full validation cycle; if the spurious rerun fails (moved base, flake), the freshly re-stamped red hands the PR to `fail_validation` and it gets parked — the rule actively harms the PRs it protects. Same trap after the rule's own remedy: attempt-1 cancelled check runs persist next to attempt-2's, so any tick where the marker read errors (`catch` → `rcReported = false`) re-fires.

Fix (~5 lines): keep only the **latest** check run per required context (max `completed_at`, tie-break by `id`) before testing `=== 'CANCELLED'`, and add a test fixture with a stale-cancelled + fresh-green pair (the current fixtures only ever carry the cancelled runs, which pins the bug).

---

### Thread 2 — `js/smAgent.js`

**ai-teammate** (2026-10-04):
⚠️ **IMPORTANT: once-per-head marker is posted even when the rerun set covers only part of the cancelled contexts**

`rcTargets` can legitimately cover a **subset** of `rcCancelled`: contexts whose cancelled runs are already attempt-2+ (skipped by design), or whose job names don't match any walked run (`jobs?per_page=50` cap, job-name/context drift). The marker is then posted anyway, and from the next tick on the `rcReported` check short-circuits **before** the mapping probe — the head is "remedied" forever while the uncovered contexts still read `CANCELLED` (the exact gh-682 BLOCKED symptom), and even the per-tick `"no rerunnable ... skip"` warn disappears into the marker.

```js
if (rcReported) {
    console.log('  ⏭️  ' + key + ' cancelled checks already re-run for head — waiting on the rerun');
    continue;
}
```

Suggestion: post the marker only when `rcTargets` covers **all** of `rcCancelled` (or list the uncovered contexts in the marker text), so an unmapped context keeps visibly retrying/warning instead of being silently latched shut by a partial remediation. Test to add: two cancelled contexts where only one maps to an attempt-1 run → no marker on that tick.

---

### Thread 3 — `js/unit-tests/test_smAgent.js`

**ai-teammate** (2026-10-04):
⚠️ **IMPORTANT: copy-paste bug in the new test helper — `it[k] = extra` drops the `[k]` index**

```js
function prItem682(n, extra) {
    var it = { key: 'pr-' + n, labels: ['ai_validating'], issueNumber: null,
               prNumber: n, draft: false, branch: 'ai/gh-1202',
               pr: { headSha: '898efd4' } };
    if (extra) { for (var k in extra) { if (extra.hasOwnProperty(k)) it[k] = extra; } }
    return it;
}
```

Every sibling helper in this file does `it[k] = extra[k]` (lines 855, 1682, 1864, 2041) — this copy assigns the whole `extra` object to every key. It is latent today only because every call site is `prItem682(1202)`; the first caller that passes `extra` (e.g. `prItem682(1202, { labels: ['ai_validated'] })`) gets `{ labels: {labels: [...]}, prNumber: {labels: [...]}, ... }` and a silently wrong fixture. One-character fix.

---

### Thread 4 — `js/smAgent.js`

**ai-teammate** (2026-10-04):
💡 **SUGGESTION: `number:` vs `pullRequestId:` — keep one spelling per tool in this file**

This new call site passes `number: ticket.prNumber` to `github_get_pr_comments`, while all 8 other call sites in this file (1573, 1817, 1845, 1993, 2020, 2165, 2979 …) use `pullRequestId:`. Both aliases work against the current dmtools runtime (verified live), but if the tool ever tightens its input schema, every site should already agree — `pullRequestId` is the canonical name per `js/common/trackers.js` ("the number argument keeps the tool's canonical pullRequestId name"). Same payload, just match the file's existing contract.

---

### Thread 5 — `js/smAgent.js`

**ai-teammate** (2026-10-04):
💡 **SUGGESTION: `rcRunIds` is dead code**

```js
var rcRunIds = [];
var rcSeen = {};
rcTargets.forEach(function (t) {
    if (rcSeen[t.runId]) return;
    rcSeen[t.runId] = true;
    rcRunIds.push(t.runId);
```

`rcRunIds` is populated and never read — `rcSeen` alone performs the per-run dedup (and the log line below re-derives the summary from `rcTargets`). Drop the array; less state to misread in an already guard-dense block.

---

### Thread 6 — `js/smAgent.js`

**ai-teammate** (2026-10-04):
💡 **SUGGESTION: both probes cap at `per_page=50` — busy heads can silently exceed the window**

`headWorkflowRuns` (this line) and the per-run jobs probe (line 2774) stop at 50. A long-lived PR head accumulates runs on every push × workflow (the gh-682 evidence alone shows 8+ kicker runs in one 36-second wave), and `actions/runs?head_sha=` returns newest-first — so on a sufficiently busy head the cancelled run can fall outside the first page. Failure mode is quiet: the context still reads `CANCELLED` via the check-runs endpoint, but `rerunTargetsForCancelledContexts` finds no run → `⚠️ ... no rerunnable (attempt-1) cancelled run — skip, retry next tick` forever (no remedy, no marker). Either raise/page the cap for this targeted probe (a filtered `runs?head_sha=` + `conclusion=cancelled` server-side would shrink the payload too), or log the total_count when the window is saturated so the gap is visible.

---

### Thread 7 — `sm_github.json`

**ai-teammate** (2026-10-04):
💡 **SUGGESTION: `limit: 1` drains a cancel-wave one PR per 10-min tick**

The action itself is cheap (a few API reads + an idempotent `gh run rerun` — no workflow dispatch, no budget competition), but the gh-682 evidence shows eight branches' kickers cancelled inside one 36-second wave. At `limit: 1` on the 10-minute SM cadence that wave needs ~80 minutes to drain, with `ai_validated` queue-heads stuck BLOCKED the whole time — the dead-zone cost this PR is trying to eliminate. The sibling bulk rules use `limit: 10` (`sweep-stale-validating`, `silent-update-behind`); consider matching them, the guards (marker, in-flight probe, attempt-1-only) already bound the write side.

## Conventions

### No project-specific content — STRICT RULE

**This is a public, product-agnostic repository. NEVER commit anything company- or customer-specific here.** Violations are a fireable offense and require history rewrite.

Forbidden anywhere in this repo (code, comments, prompts, instructions, tests, docs, commit messages):

- Company, customer, or product names
- Internal hostnames, URLs, IPs, Jira/Confluence links, real ticket keys
- Internal label/branch/repo naming conventions tied to one organization
- File paths pointing to internal repos, internal registry URLs
- Sample data copied from real internal systems

Everything here must be **generic and configurable**: names like `example.com`, `PROJ-123`, `acme`; behavior driven by `customParams` / `.dmtools/config.js` in the consuming repo. Project context goes in the target repo's `.dmtools/config.js` or the corporate orchestrator repo — never here.

**Before every commit**: re-read your diff and check it against this list.

### Agent config structure
- `metadata.contextId` identifies the workflow (used for config composition lookups).
- `preJSAction` / `preCliJSAction` / `postJSAction` — GraalJS hooks that run before/after the CLI agent.
- `cliPrompt` — path to the main prompt markdown.
- `cliPrompts` — additional prompt files appended to the CLI agent input.
- `cliCommands` — shell scripts invoked by dmtools to run the AI CLI.

### Label-based idempotency

# Pull Request Information

- **PR #**: 695
- **URL**: https://github.com/IstiN/dmtools-agents/pull/695
- **Title**: gh-682: standing SM remedy — cancelled required checks re-run themselves (kicker cancel-loop)
- **Author**: IstiN
- **Branch**: `fix/682-rerun-cancelled-checks` → `main`
- **State**: open
- **Files Changed**: 4
- **Additions**: +617
- **Deletions**: -1
- **Created**: 2026-10-04T06:56:26Z
- **Updated**: 2026-10-04T07:54:58Z

## PR Description

Closes #682 (PR 1 of 2 — the kicker-side fix lands in IstiN/dmtools-agentic-workflows; this PR is the standing SM remedy + this repo's own stub scoping).

## Evidence (#682)

- **fa#1202** (head `898efd4`): all 4 kicker push-runs on `ai/gh-1171` CANCELLED 21:43–23:05 as silent-refresh pushes landed; required checks ended CANCELLED → PR BLOCKED until the manual rerun at 23:26.
- **fa#1203**: same pattern twice (23:47, 23:57) — the queue head stalled on it.
- **Still reproducing 2026-10-04 06:21–06:22**: eight branches' kicker runs cancelled inside one 36-second dev-wave (fa run ids 37182568709…37182598010); this repo's own kicker showed the same at 06:36/06:41/06:43.
- Cost on 2026-10-03 alone: 2 dead zones on queue heads + 2 manual reruns.

Mechanism: a queued run in a shared concurrency group **always supersedes the pending one** — *"Any existing pending job or workflow in the same concurrency group, if it exists, will be canceled and the new queued job or workflow will take its place"* (GitHub docs). `cancel-in-progress: false` only shields the RUNNING run. Every silent-refresh push therefore killed the pending kicker, and no rule treated CANCELLED as re-runnable (the #632 class, now triggered by our own refresh machinery).

## What this PR does

**1. Standing rule `rerun-cancelled-checks`** (`sm_github.json`, FIRST in the array):

- match: armed (`ai_validating`) or latched (`ai_validated`) PR; not BEHIND (silent-update refreshes that head), not DIRTY (conflict-rework owns it), not `agent:rework`;
- `localAction rerun_cancelled_checks` (js/smAgent.js):
  - scans the head's check runs — only contexts that currently read **CANCELLED** among `rule.requiredContexts` act (dart: `static`/`gate`/`agents-gate`; fa: the kicker's `kicker / sm-liveness`, `kicker / head-completeness`). Failure paths untouched — red stays `fail_validation` territory;
  - once-per-head marker comment (conflict_rework pacing) citing fa#1202/#1203 + 2026-10-04 06:21, posted AFTER the reruns land (the gh-683 bug C invariant: a failed rerun posts no marker, the next tick retries);
  - **no in-flight run on the head** guard — the `hasActiveDispatchedRun` probe pattern widened to every run on the head (any event): an active run re-stamps the contexts by itself;
  - `gh run rerun <id>` of the latest **attempt-1** cancelled run per required context (deduped per run id); a run already re-run and still cancelled is skipped — no automatic retry loop.
- Placement: it never touches labels and never dispatches workflows, so it **cannot fight `sweep-stale-validating`** (cancelled conclusions never sweep by design anyway); the documented #637 invariant (merge-validated before sweep) is preserved by prefixing, never interleaving.

**2. This repo's own kicker stub** (`.github/workflows/factory-sm-kicker.yml`): the caller-level global `sm-kicker` group alone would keep superseding pending kickers even after the canonical awf fix is re-pinned — scoped to `sm-kicker-${{ github.sha }}` (effective once the pin bump lands; pin bumps are separate PRs by repo convention).

## Tests

10 new unit tests in the existing `test_smAgent.js` rule-test patterns (rerun+marker shape, rerun-failure posts no marker, CANCELLED-only matching, in-flight skip, once-per-head pacing, attempt-2 no-loop, newest-run-wins, dry-run, no-config skip, and a `sm_github.json` placement pin asserting rule order). Node harness: 178 passed, 1 failed — the single failure is the pre-existing `assert.doesNotThrow` mock gap present on clean `main` (the canonical gate is the pack-release test job). `actionlint` clean. #684/#685/#686 suites untouched and green.

# PR Discussion History

_Previous review discussions for PR #695._

## Review Threads (Inline Comments)

### Thread 1 — `js/smAgent.js`

**ai-teammate** (2026-10-04):
🚨 **BLOCKING: the scan flags a required context as CANCELLED even when a NEWER run already re-stamped it green**

`cancelledRequiredContexts` treats the context as cancelled if **any** check run in the commit's rollup reads `CANCELLED`:

```js
rollup.forEach(function (r) {
    var name = r && (r.name || r.context);
    var concl = r && r.conclusion ? String(r.conclusion).toUpperCase() : null;
    if (name && concl === 'CANCELLED' && contexts.indexOf(name) !== -1) {
        cancelled[name] = true;
    }
});
```

`github_get_commit_check_runs` returns **all** check runs on the commit (verified live: "Get all check runs ... for a commit SHA") — including stale ones from earlier attempts/dispatches. Branch protection resolves each required context by its **latest** check run; this code does not, despite the comment claiming "the check-runs rollup is the source of truth".

Reachable sequence with this repo's own machinery:

1. Validation run A (attempt 1) on head H is cancelled — exactly the #632/#682 class this rule targets (or stale-run cleanup).
2. `revalidate-armed` re-dispatches a fresh run B on H after the 15-min grace → B re-stamps `static`/`gate`/`agents-gate` **green**.
3. Next tick this rule runs **first** (before `merge-validated`), sees A's stale `CANCELLED` check runs, and `gh run rerun`s A + posts the marker — on a head that is already green and mergeable.

Consequences: the merge is delayed a full validation cycle; if the spurious rerun fails (moved base, flake), the freshly re-stamped red hands the PR to `fail_validation` and it gets parked — the rule actively harms the PRs it protects. Same trap after the rule's own remedy: attempt-1 cancelled check runs persist next to attempt-2's, so any tick where the marker read errors (`catch` → `rcReported = false`) re-fires.

Fix (~5 lines): keep only the **latest** check run per required context (max `completed_at`, tie-break by `id`) before testing `=== 'CANCELLED'`, and add a test fixture with a stale-cancelled + fresh-green pair (the current fixtures only ever carry the cancelled runs, which pins the bug).

---

### Thread 2 — `js/smAgent.js`

**ai-teammate** (2026-10-04):
⚠️ **IMPORTANT: once-per-head marker is posted even when the rerun set covers only part of the cancelled contexts**

`rcTargets` can legitimately cover a **subset** of `rcCancelled`: contexts whose cancelled runs are already attempt-2+ (skipped by design), or whose job names don't match any walked run (`jobs?per_page=50` cap, job-name/context drift). The marker is then posted anyway, and from the next tick on the `rcReported` check short-circuits **before** the mapping probe — the head is "remedied" forever while the uncovered contexts still read `CANCELLED` (the exact gh-682 BLOCKED symptom), and even the per-tick `"no rerunnable ... skip"` warn disappears into the marker.

```js
if (rcReported) {
    console.log('  ⏭️  ' + key + ' cancelled checks already re-run for head — waiting on the rerun');
    continue;
}
```

Suggestion: post the marker only when `rcTargets` covers **all** of `rcCancelled` (or list the uncovered contexts in the marker text), so an unmapped context keeps visibly retrying/warning instead of being silently latched shut by a partial remediation. Test to add: two cancelled contexts where only one maps to an attempt-1 run → no marker on that tick.

---

### Thread 3 — `js/unit-tests/test_smAgent.js`

**ai-teammate** (2026-10-04):
⚠️ **IMPORTANT: copy-paste bug in the new test helper — `it[k] = extra` drops the `[k]` index**

```js
function prItem682(n, extra) {
    var it = { key: 'pr-' + n, labels: ['ai_validating'], issueNumber: null,
               prNumber: n, draft: false, branch: 'ai/gh-1202',
               pr: { headSha: '898efd4' } };
    if (extra) { for (var k in extra) { if (extra.hasOwnProperty(k)) it[k] = extra; } }
    return it;
}
```

Every sibling helper in this file does `it[k] = extra[k]` (lines 855, 1682, 1864, 2041) — this copy assigns the whole `extra` object to every key. It is latent today only because every call site is `prItem682(1202)`; the first caller that passes `extra` (e.g. `prItem682(1202, { labels: ['ai_validated'] })`) gets `{ labels: {labels: [...]}, prNumber: {labels: [...]}, ... }` and a silently wrong fixture. One-character fix.

---

### Thread 4 — `js/smAgent.js`

**ai-teammate** (2026-10-04):
💡 **SUGGESTION: `number:` vs `pullRequestId:` — keep one spelling per tool in this file**

This new call site passes `number: ticket.prNumber` to `github_get_pr_comments`, while all 8 other call sites in this file (1573, 1817, 1845, 1993, 2020, 2165, 2979 …) use `pullRequestId:`. Both aliases work against the current dmtools runtime (verified live), but if the tool ever tightens its input schema, every site should already agree — `pullRequestId` is the canonical name per `js/common/trackers.js` ("the number argument keeps the tool's canonical pullRequestId name"). Same payload, just match the file's existing contract.

---

### Thread 5 — `js/smAgent.js`

**ai-teammate** (2026-10-04):
💡 **SUGGESTION: `rcRunIds` is dead code**

```js
var rcRunIds = [];
var rcSeen = {};
rcTargets.forEach(function (t) {
    if (rcSeen[t.runId]) return;
    rcSeen[t.runId] = true;
    rcRunIds.push(t.runId);
```

`rcRunIds` is populated and never read — `rcSeen` alone performs the per-run dedup (and the log line below re-derives the summary from `rcTargets`). Drop the array; less state to misread in an already guard-dense block.

---

### Thread 6 — `js/smAgent.js`

**ai-teammate** (2026-10-04):
💡 **SUGGESTION: both probes cap at `per_page=50` — busy heads can silently exceed the window**

`headWorkflowRuns` (this line) and the per-run jobs probe (line 2774) stop at 50. A long-lived PR head accumulates runs on every push × workflow (the gh-682 evidence alone shows 8+ kicker runs in one 36-second wave), and `actions/runs?head_sha=` returns newest-first — so on a sufficiently busy head the cancelled run can fall outside the first page. Failure mode is quiet: the context still reads `CANCELLED` via the check-runs endpoint, but `rerunTargetsForCancelledContexts` finds no run → `⚠️ ... no rerunnable (attempt-1) cancelled run — skip, retry next tick` forever (no remedy, no marker). Either raise/page the cap for this targeted probe (a filtered `runs?head_sha=` + `conclusion=cancelled` server-side would shrink the payload too), or log the total_count when the window is saturated so the gap is visible.

---

### Thread 7 — `sm_github.json`

**ai-teammate** (2026-10-04):
💡 **SUGGESTION: `limit: 1` drains a cancel-wave one PR per 10-min tick**

The action itself is cheap (a few API reads + an idempotent `gh run rerun` — no workflow dispatch, no budget competition), but the gh-682 evidence shows eight branches' kickers cancelled inside one 36-second wave. At `limit: 1` on the 10-minute SM cadence that wave needs ~80 minutes to drain, with `ai_validated` queue-heads stuck BLOCKED the whole time — the dead-zone cost this PR is trying to eliminate. The sibling bulk rules use `limit: 10` (`sweep-stale-validating`, `silent-update-behind`); consider matching them, the guards (marker, in-flight probe, attempt-1-only) already bound the write side.

**Key Issues**:
- 🚨 `js/smAgent.js:2733` — stale check-run matching; fix = latest-check-run-per-context before the `CANCELLED` test (+ fixture with stale-cancelled + fresh-green pair)

surface ALL remaining issues"] EXHAUST --> OUTPUT["8. Write outputs:
pr_review.json · pr_review_general.md · pr_review_comments/*.md"] OUTPUT --> END([End]) ``` ## 1. Input context — MANDATORY reading order ```mermaid flowchart TD subgraph PR_CONTEXT["⚠️ PR-specific files (read first)"] P1["1️⃣ instruction.md (repo root) — project stack, conventions"] P2["2️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_info.md — PR title, author, branch, description"] P3["3️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_diff.txt — the diff to review"] P4["4️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_files.txt — list of changed files"] P5["5️⃣ input/TICKET/ci_failures.md — CI failures = BLOCKING (last 500 lines)"] P5_FULL["5️⃣ input/TICKET/ci_failures_full.log — full CI logs"] P6["6️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_discussions.md + pr_discussions_raw.json — existing comments"] P1 --> P2 --> P3 --> P4 --> P5 --> P5_FULL --> P6 end subgraph TICKET_CONTEXT["Ticket context (for understanding PR purpose)"] T1["7️⃣ input/TICKET/ticket.md — linked ticket description, ACs"] T2["8️⃣ input/TICKET/comments.md — ticket discussion if present"] T3["9️⃣ input/TICKET/parent-*.md — parent story context"] T4["🔟 input/TICKET/confluence/*.md — linked specifications"] T1 --> T2 --> T3 --> T4 end subgraph RULE["⚠️ Rule"] R1["If file exists in input/ → read locally, do NOT re-fetch via dmtools"] end PR_CONTEXT --> TICKET_CONTEXT --> RULE ``` Read PR files to understand WHAT changed. Read ticket files to understand WHY it changed and verify against requirements. ## 2. Diff checklist — apply to `pr_diff.txt` For every hunk, ask at least these questions: - [ ] Does the change match the ticket scope? Any scope creep? - [ ] Are new or changed public APIs contract-safe for existing callers? - [ ] Is user/external input validated, sanitized, or escaped? - [ ] Are secrets, tokens, or PATs handled safely — not logged, not interpolated into shell scripts? - [ ] Are new or modified files present under `testing/` in a non-test-automation PR? - [ ] Is dead code, unused imports, or obvious duplication introduced? - [ ] Are error paths handled, or are failures silently swallowed? - [ ] Are new dependencies justified and compatible with the existing stack? - [ ] Beyond blockers: what other maintainability, correctness, or quality improvements are visible in the changed code? ## 3. Changed-file deep read Do not review from the diff alone. Read the full content of every changed file: - imports and dependencies - class/method responsibilities and adherence to SRP / OOP principles - naming consistency with the rest of the codebase - error handling, logging, and edge cases - test coverage for changed behavior - backward-compatibility and migration impact ## 4. Impact analysis (CodeGraph or grep fallback) Use CodeGraph to find "what could break": - `codegraph_callers` / `codegraph_callees` on modified public symbols - `codegraph_search` for: `PAT_TOKEN`, `secrets.`, `github.token`, `previousViewModel` - `codegraph_impact` before flagging architectural changes **If CodeGraph unavailable**, use grep and document it: ```bash grep -rn "changedFunctionName" --include="*.ts" . grep -rn "secrets\.\|github\.token" . ``` ## 5. Review dimensions Rate the PR across all relevant dimensions: | Dimension | What to check | |---|---| | **Security** | injection, unsafe interpolation, secret leakage, missing permissions, unsafe defaults | | **Architecture / OOP** | SRP, coupling, abstraction consistency, provider/repository boundaries | | **Code quality** | naming, complexity, error handling, logging, comments | | **Tests** | coverage for new/changed paths, meaningful assertions, no brittle string-only tests | | **Duplication** | copy-paste, duplicated logic across files, duplicated configuration | | **Backward compatibility** | public API changes, migration paths, default behavior | | **Performance** | unnecessary rebuilds, heavy sync operations, missing timeouts | | **Workflow / CI safety** | (when `.github/workflows/` changes) secret declarations, ref pinning, permissions, timeouts | ## 6. Severity classification Classify every finding before writing outputs: - **BLOCKING** — merge would cause a bug, security issue, data loss, or CI break. Must be fixed. - **IMPORTANT** — real maintainability or correctness issue. Strongly prefer fixing before merge. - **SUGGESTION** — optional improvement, style, or future polish. Does not block merge. When in doubt, start one level higher; downgrade only after confirming the risk is negligible. ## 7. Exhaustive single-pass review Treat **every** review as the final and only review pass. The author will not get another chance to catch missed findings cheaply. - Do not defer SUGGESTION or IMPORTANT items to a later round because a BLOCKING issue exists. - After classifying all findings, re-read every changed file and ask: *"What else is improvable here?"* - Before writing outputs, verify that no obvious quality, maintainability, or correctness issue was left unreported. - Aim to surface the maximum number of actionable findings in this single iteration. ## 8. # Pull Request Information

- **PR #**: 695
- **URL**: https://github.com/IstiN/dmtools-agents/pull/695
- **Title**: gh-682: standing SM remedy — cancelled required checks re-run themselves (kicker cancel-loop)
- **Author**: IstiN
- **Branch**: `fix/682-rerun-cancelled-checks` → `main`
- **State**: open
- **Files Changed**: 4
- **Additions**: +617
- **Deletions**: -1
- **Created**: 2026-10-04T06:56:26Z
- **Updated**: 2026-10-04T07:54:58Z

## PR Description

Closes #682 (PR 1 of 2 — the kicker-side fix lands in IstiN/dmtools-agentic-workflows; this PR is the standing SM remedy + this repo's own stub scoping).

## Evidence (#682)

- **fa#1202** (head `898efd4`): all 4 kicker push-runs on `ai/gh-1171` CANCELLED 21:43–23:05 as silent-refresh pushes landed; required checks ended CANCELLED → PR BLOCKED until the manual rerun at 23:26.
- **fa#1203**: same pattern twice (23:47, 23:57) — the queue head stalled on it.
- **Still reproducing 2026-10-04 06:21–06:22**: eight branches' kicker runs cancelled inside one 36-second dev-wave (fa run ids 37182568709…37182598010); this repo's own kicker showed the same at 06:36/06:41/06:43.
- Cost on 2026-10-03 alone: 2 dead zones on queue heads + 2 manual reruns.

Mechanism: a queued run in a shared concurrency group **always supersedes the pending one** — *"Any existing pending job or workflow in the same concurrency group, if it exists, will be canceled and the new queued job or workflow will take its place"* (GitHub docs). `cancel-in-progress: false` only shields the RUNNING run. Every silent-refresh push therefore killed the pending kicker, and no rule treated CANCELLED as re-runnable (the #632 class, now triggered by our own refresh machinery).

## What this PR does

**1. Standing rule `rerun-cancelled-checks`** (`sm_github.json`, FIRST in the array):

- match: armed (`ai_validating`) or latched (`ai_validated`) PR; not BEHIND (silent-update refreshes that head), not DIRTY (conflict-rework owns it), not `agent:rework`;
- `localAction rerun_cancelled_checks` (js/smAgent.js):
  - scans the head's check runs — only contexts that currently read **CANCELLED** among `rule.requiredContexts` act (dart: `static`/`gate`/`agents-gate`; fa: the kicker's `kicker / sm-liveness`, `kicker / head-completeness`). Failure paths untouched — red stays `fail_validation` territory;
  - once-per-head marker comment (conflict_rework pacing) citing fa#1202/#1203 + 2026-10-04 06:21, posted AFTER the reruns land (the gh-683 bug C invariant: a failed rerun posts no marker, the next tick retries);
  - **no in-flight run on the head** guard — the `hasActiveDispatchedRun` probe pattern widened to every run on the head (any event): an active run re-stamps the contexts by itself;
  - `gh run rerun <id>` of the latest **attempt-1** cancelled run per required context (deduped per run id); a run already re-run and still cancelled is skipped — no automatic retry loop.
- Placement: it never touches labels and never dispatches workflows, so it **cannot fight `sweep-stale-validating`** (cancelled conclusions never sweep by design anyway); the documented #637 invariant (merge-validated before sweep) is preserved by prefixing, never interleaving.

**2. This repo's own kicker stub** (`.github/workflows/factory-sm-kicker.yml`): the caller-level global `sm-kicker` group alone would keep superseding pending kickers even after the canonical awf fix is re-pinned — scoped to `sm-kicker-${{ github.sha }}` (effective once the pin bump lands; pin bumps are separate PRs by repo convention).

## Tests

10 new unit tests in the existing `test_smAgent.js` rule-test patterns (rerun+marker shape, rerun-failure posts no marker, CANCELLED-only matching, in-flight skip, once-per-head pacing, attempt-2 no-loop, newest-run-wins, dry-run, no-config skip, and a `sm_github.json` placement pin asserting rule order). Node harness: 178 passed, 1 failed — the single failure is the pre-existing `assert.doesNotThrow` mock gap present on clean `main` (the canonical gate is the pack-release test job). `actionlint` clean. #684/#685/#686 suites untouched and green.

# PR Discussion History

_Previous review discussions for PR #695._

## Review Threads (Inline Comments)

### Thread 1 — `js/smAgent.js`

**ai-teammate** (2026-10-04):
🚨 **BLOCKING: the scan flags a required context as CANCELLED even when a NEWER run already re-stamped it green**

`cancelledRequiredContexts` treats the context as cancelled if **any** check run in the commit's rollup reads `CANCELLED`:

```js
rollup.forEach(function (r) {
    var name = r && (r.name || r.context);
    var concl = r && r.conclusion ? String(r.conclusion).toUpperCase() : null;
    if (name && concl === 'CANCELLED' && contexts.indexOf(name) !== -1) {
        cancelled[name] = true;
    }
});
```

`github_get_commit_check_runs` returns **all** check runs on the commit (verified live: "Get all check runs ... for a commit SHA") — including stale ones from earlier attempts/dispatches. Branch protection resolves each required context by its **latest** check run; this code does not, despite the comment claiming "the check-runs rollup is the source of truth".

Reachable sequence with this repo's own machinery:

1. Validation run A (attempt 1) on head H is cancelled — exactly the #632/#682 class this rule targets (or stale-run cleanup).
2. `revalidate-armed` re-dispatches a fresh run B on H after the 15-min grace → B re-stamps `static`/`gate`/`agents-gate` **green**.
3. Next tick this rule runs **first** (before `merge-validated`), sees A's stale `CANCELLED` check runs, and `gh run rerun`s A + posts the marker — on a head that is already green and mergeable.

Consequences: the merge is delayed a full validation cycle; if the spurious rerun fails (moved base, flake), the freshly re-stamped red hands the PR to `fail_validation` and it gets parked — the rule actively harms the PRs it protects. Same trap after the rule's own remedy: attempt-1 cancelled check runs persist next to attempt-2's, so any tick where the marker read errors (`catch` → `rcReported = false`) re-fires.

Fix (~5 lines): keep only the **latest** check run per required context (max `completed_at`, tie-break by `id`) before testing `=== 'CANCELLED'`, and add a test fixture with a stale-cancelled + fresh-green pair (the current fixtures only ever carry the cancelled runs, which pins the bug).

---

### Thread 2 — `js/smAgent.js`

**ai-teammate** (2026-10-04):
⚠️ **IMPORTANT: once-per-head marker is posted even when the rerun set covers only part of the cancelled contexts**

`rcTargets` can legitimately cover a **subset** of `rcCancelled`: contexts whose cancelled runs are already attempt-2+ (skipped by design), or whose job names don't match any walked run (`jobs?per_page=50` cap, job-name/context drift). The marker is then posted anyway, and from the next tick on the `rcReported` check short-circuits **before** the mapping probe — the head is "remedied" forever while the uncovered contexts still read `CANCELLED` (the exact gh-682 BLOCKED symptom), and even the per-tick `"no rerunnable ... skip"` warn disappears into the marker.

```js
if (rcReported) {
    console.log('  ⏭️  ' + key + ' cancelled checks already re-run for head — waiting on the rerun');
    continue;
}
```

Suggestion: post the marker only when `rcTargets` covers **all** of `rcCancelled` (or list the uncovered contexts in the marker text), so an unmapped context keeps visibly retrying/warning instead of being silently latched shut by a partial remediation. Test to add: two cancelled contexts where only one maps to an attempt-1 run → no marker on that tick.

---

### Thread 3 — `js/unit-tests/test_smAgent.js`

**ai-teammate** (2026-10-04):
⚠️ **IMPORTANT: copy-paste bug in the new test helper — `it[k] = extra` drops the `[k]` index**

```js
function prItem682(n, extra) {
    var it = { key: 'pr-' + n, labels: ['ai_validating'], issueNumber: null,
               prNumber: n, draft: false, branch: 'ai/gh-1202',
               pr: { headSha: '898efd4' } };
    if (extra) { for (var k in extra) { if (extra.hasOwnProperty(k)) it[k] = extra; } }
    return it;
}
```

Every sibling helper in this file does `it[k] = extra[k]` (lines 855, 1682, 1864, 2041) — this copy assigns the whole `extra` object to every key. It is latent today only because every call site is `prItem682(1202)`; the first caller that passes `extra` (e.g. `prItem682(1202, { labels: ['ai_validated'] })`) gets `{ labels: {labels: [...]}, prNumber: {labels: [...]}, ... }` and a silently wrong fixture. One-character fix.

---

### Thread 4 — `js/smAgent.js`

**ai-teammate** (2026-10-04):
💡 **SUGGESTION: `number:` vs `pullRequestId:` — keep one spelling per tool in this file**

This new call site passes `number: ticket.prNumber` to `github_get_pr_comments`, while all 8 other call sites in this file (1573, 1817, 1845, 1993, 2020, 2165, 2979 …) use `pullRequestId:`. Both aliases work against the current dmtools runtime (verified live), but if the tool ever tightens its input schema, every site should already agree — `pullRequestId` is the canonical name per `js/common/trackers.js` ("the number argument keeps the tool's canonical pullRequestId name"). Same payload, just match the file's existing contract.

---

### Thread 5 — `js/smAgent.js`

**ai-teammate** (2026-10-04):
💡 **SUGGESTION: `rcRunIds` is dead code**

```js
var rcRunIds = [];
var rcSeen = {};
rcTargets.forEach(function (t) {
    if (rcSeen[t.runId]) return;
    rcSeen[t.runId] = true;
    rcRunIds.push(t.runId);
```

`rcRunIds` is populated and never read — `rcSeen` alone performs the per-run dedup (and the log line below re-derives the summary from `rcTargets`). Drop the array; less state to misread in an already guard-dense block.

---

### Thread 6 — `js/smAgent.js`

**ai-teammate** (2026-10-04):
💡 **SUGGESTION: both probes cap at `per_page=50` — busy heads can silently exceed the window**

`headWorkflowRuns` (this line) and the per-run jobs probe (line 2774) stop at 50. A long-lived PR head accumulates runs on every push × workflow (the gh-682 evidence alone shows 8+ kicker runs in one 36-second wave), and `actions/runs?head_sha=` returns newest-first — so on a sufficiently busy head the cancelled run can fall outside the first page. Either raise/page the cap for this targeted probe (a filtered `runs?head_sha=` + `conclusion=cancelled` server-side would shrink the payload too), or log the total_count when the window is saturated so the gap is visible.

---

### Thread 7 — `sm_github.json`

**ai-teammate** (2026-10-04):
💡 **SUGGESTION: `limit: 1` drains a cancel-wave one PR per 10-min tick**

The action itself is cheap (a few API reads + an idempotent `gh run rerun` — no workflow dispatch, no budget competition), but the gh-682 evidence shows eight branches' kickers cancelled inside one 36-second wave. At `limit: 1` on the 10-minute SM cadence that wave needs ~80 minutes to drain, with `ai_validated` queue-heads stuck BLOCKED the whole time — the dead-zone cost this PR is trying to eliminate. The sibling bulk rules use `limit: 10` (`sweep-stale-validating`, `silent-update-behind`); consider matching them, the guards (marker, in-flight probe, attempt-1-only) already bound the write side.

## Conventions

### No project-specific content — STRICT RULE

**This is a public, product-agnostic repository. NEVER commit anything company- or customer-specific here.** Violations are a fireable offense and require history rewrite.

Forbidden anywhere in this repo (code, comments, prompts, instructions, tests, docs, commit messages):

- Company, customer, or product names
- Internal hostnames, URLs, IPs, Jira/Confluence links, real ticket keys
- Internal label/branch/repo naming conventions tied to one organization
- File paths pointing to internal repos, internal registry URLs
- Sample data copied from real internal systems

Everything here must be **generic and configurable**: names like `example.com`, `PROJ-123`, `acme`; behavior driven by `customParams` / `.dmtools/config.js` in the consuming repo. Project context goes in the target repo's `.dmtools/config.js` or the corporate orchestrator repo — never here.

**Before every commit**: re-read your diff and check it against this list.

### Agent config structure
- `metadata.contextId` identifies the workflow (used for config composition lookups).
- `preJSAction` / `preCliJSAction` / `postJSAction` — GraalJS hooks that run before/after the CLI agent.
- `cliPrompt` — path to the main prompt markdown.
- `cliPrompts` — additional prompt files appended to the CLI agent input.
- `cliCommands` — shell scripts invoked by dmtools to run the AI CLI.

### Label-based idempotency

Read ticket files to understand WHY it changed and verify against requirements. ## 2. Diff checklist — apply to `pr_diff.txt` For every hunk, ask at least these questions: - [ ] Does the change match the ticket scope? Any scope creep? - [ ] Are new or changed public APIs contract-safe for existing callers? - [ ] Is user/external input validated, sanitized, or escaped? - [ ] Are secrets, tokens, or PATs handled safely — not logged, not interpolated into shell scripts? - [ ] Are new or modified files present under `testing/` in a non-test-automation PR? - [ ] Is dead code, unused imports, or obvious duplication introduced? - [ ] Are error paths handled, or are failures silently swallowed? - [ ] Are new dependencies justified and compatible with the existing stack? - [ ] Beyond blockers: what other maintainability, correctness, or quality improvements are visible in the changed code? ## 3. Changed-file deep read Do not review from the diff alone. Read the full content of every changed file: - imports and dependencies - class/method responsibilities and adherence to SRP / OOP principles - naming consistency with the rest of the codebase - error handling, logging, and edge cases - test coverage for changed behavior - backward-compatibility and migration impact ## 4. Impact analysis (CodeGraph or grep fallback) Use CodeGraph to find "what could break": - `codegraph_callers` / `codegraph_callees` on modified public symbols - `codegraph_search` for: `PAT_TOKEN`, `secrets.`, `github.token`, `previousViewModel` - `codegraph_impact` before flagging architectural changes **If CodeGraph unavailable**, use grep and document it: ```bash grep -rn "changedFunctionName" --include="*.ts" . grep -rn "secrets\.\|github\.token" . ``` ## 5. Must be fixed. - **IMPORTANT** — real maintainability or correctness issue. Strongly prefer fixing before merge. - **SUGGESTION** — optional improvement, style, or future polish. Does not block merge. When in doubt, start one level higher; downgrade only after confirming the risk is negligible. ## 7. Exhaustive single-pass review Treat **every** review as the final and only review pass. The author will not get another chance to catch missed findings cheaply. - Do not defer SUGGESTION or IMPORTANT items to a later round because a BLOCKING issue exists. - After classifying all findings, re-read every changed file and ask: *"What else is improvable here?"* - Before writing outputs, verify that no obvious quality, maintainability, or correctness issue was left unreported. - Aim to surface the maximum number of actionable findings in this single iteration. ## 8. If `pr_diff.txt` is truncated, run `git diff origin/{baseBranch}...HEAD` to locate the correct line numbers. # Pull Request Information

- **PR #**: 695
- **URL**: https://github.com/IstiN/dmtools-agents/pull/695
- **Title**: gh-682: standing SM remedy — cancelled required checks re-run themselves (kicker cancel-loop)
- **Author**: IstiN
- **Branch**: `fix/682-rerun-cancelled-checks` → `main`
- **State**: open
- **Files Changed**: 4
- **Additions**: +617
- **Deletions**: -1
- **Created**: 2026-10-04T06:56:26Z
- **Updated**: 2026-10-04T07:54:58Z

## PR Description

Closes #682 (PR 1 of 2 — the kicker-side fix lands in IstiN/dmtools-agentic-workflows; this PR is the standing SM remedy + this repo's own stub scoping).

## Evidence (#682)

- **fa#1202** (head `898efd4`): all 4 kicker push-runs on `ai/gh-1171` CANCELLED 21:43–23:05 as silent-refresh pushes landed; required checks ended CANCELLED → PR BLOCKED until the manual rerun at 23:26.
- **fa#1203**: same pattern twice (23:47, 23:57) — the queue head stalled on it.
- **Still reproducing 2026-10-04 06:21–06:22**: eight branches' kicker runs cancelled inside one 36-second dev-wave (fa run ids 37182568709…37182598010); this repo's own kicker showed the same at 06:36/06:41/06:43.
- Cost on 2026-10-03 alone: 2 dead zones on queue heads + 2 manual reruns.

Mechanism: a queued run in a shared concurrency group **always supersedes the pending one** — *"Any existing pending job or workflow in the same concurrency group, if it exists, will be canceled and the new queued job or workflow will take its place"* (GitHub docs). `cancel-in-progress: false` only shields the RUNNING run. Every silent-refresh push therefore killed the pending kicker, and no rule treated CANCELLED as re-runnable (the #632 class, now triggered by our own refresh machinery).

## What this PR does

**1. Standing rule `rerun-cancelled-checks`** (`sm_github.json`, FIRST in the array):

- match: armed (`ai_validating`) or latched (`ai_validated`) PR; not BEHIND (silent-update refreshes that head), not DIRTY (conflict-rework owns it), not `agent:rework`;
- `localAction rerun_cancelled_checks` (js/smAgent.js):
